Once the infernal creatures are banished or killed, Christian burial for the victims of both Damhan-Allaidh and the Order can destroy the regio, and within a decade the place becomes a two-level magical regio (+2, +4). Digging while the Infernal regio stands draws further attacks, and many workers die in accidents (p. 94).

The map (p. 93) shows the walled fort, with four barracks, stables on two sides, a granary, the headquarters, two storehouses and a catapult platform on one corner; beyond its wall stand the bath house, the mansio and the married quarters.

neighbours.name: Glyder Fawr Sanctum
neighbours.summary: Glyder Fawr is a Welsh peak just under a thousand paces high, north of Snowdon and about ten miles east of the port of Caernarfon, off the pass of Llanberis.
neighbours.secrets:
Ealasaid's first sanctum and later Macomb's, about 100 paces under the peak in a powerful +7 magical aura. Fleeing threats from Diedne magi, she had left her Welsh home before Pralix reached Britain; when the magi of Vindolanda set up sancta far from their main site she reclaimed her ancestral lands, near Cad Gadu, and later left this one to Macomb on moving to the Sea Temple (p. 94).

A cave system lower on the southern side gives on to the passage, but the way in through Macomb's lab is blocked for about ten paces and the lab cannot be crossed (pp. 94-95). The characters will most likely come by the gatestone in Old Vindolanda (p. 95).

The aura suited Macomb's and Ealasaid's ritual magic. They advised Victor on a temple to raise the site's power further, and it did better than they hoped, but the aura proved too strong for servants to live here safely, so covenfolk never used the quarters. Macomb's apprentice had one closet when Damhan-Allaidh came (p. 95).

Macomb died quickly. His apprentice called up elemental spirits and set them on the attacker; the fight brought down most of the sanctum and drove Damhan-Allaidh off, but the apprentice was dead by then (p. 95).

The map (p. 95) shows on the upper level storage, a kitchen, a meeting hall, a latrine, a bath, servants' quarters, the gate room and the temple; on the lower level storage, vis storage, Macomb's quarters, Macomb's lab, Ealasaid's Gate, and the altar passageway.

Two earth elementals called by the apprentice remain: see Cadell and Enan.

neighbours.name: Sea Temple Sanctum
neighbours.summary: A sanctum of the covenant of Vindolanda, whose whereabouts its builder told no one.
neighbours.secrets:
Ealasaid's sanctum and the magi's last and boldest work, about eight miles due west of the isle of Lundy, under the sea between Devon and Wales. Thothian spirits led her to a magical site suited to her research on the Obsidian Gateway, on condition that she alone should know where it lay. She drove a tunnel of nearly eight miles under the sea and cast Carve the Mythic Chambers about ten paces below the seabed. The crystal dome rose from the seabed over a magical spring (pp. 94, 122-123).

Just before she died she had found the name of the spirit serving the Obsidian Gateway and had begun rebuilding its ritual. Damhan-Allaidh surprised her under the dome, her theurgy too slow to save her, and raised her ghost to torture out where Victor and Hetep were. Months later a Tremere and Flambeau force beat his army and he fled here, hurt and spent, and found Liam freeing her ghost. The two gruagachan took beast shape and fought. Even so Liam lost. When he lay incapacitated her spirit ordered an earth elemental to shatter the dome: the fall crushed both men's bodies and flooded most of the structure, and her ghost, its purpose done, rested (p. 123).

Liam and Damhan-Allaidh have lain incapacitated under the rubble for over three hundred years, sea creatures feeding on their ever-mending bodies. Chapter 18's statistics are their state if freed and left to recover. Hermetic magic at Instant duration cannot mend their distortions, though spells may give brief relief, and both slowly lose their reason (pp. 122-123).

Victor and Iain can tell the players nothing of where it lies. The way in is the gatestone at Old Vindolanda; the gatestone from Glyder Fawr is out of position (p. 123). The book also gives the trilithon from the valley (p. 96) and the exit tunnel (p. 124).

The library holds all that is needed to recreate Ealasaid's work on the Obsidian Gateway. Twenty sets of her lab notes, once translated and written up, each serve as a Quality 2 Tractatus in Occult Lore (or Theurgy, with The Mysteries), and all must be studied first. Her personal translation notes are hard going: each studies as a Summa, Quality 0, on Speak Ancient Egyptian (Level 4), Scribe Hieroglyphics (3), Speak Assyrian (3) or Scribe Cuneiform (3). Using the tablets in her lab takes at least 3 in both Speak Ancient Egyptian and Speak Assyrian and at least 2 in both Scribe Hieroglyphics and Scribe Cuneiform. The ritual must be designed at level 40 (p. 124).

Hetep frees Damhan-Allaidh here in Brighde's Gauntlet, after casting a Creo Auram spell on the chamber; the Hermetic equivalent is Sanctuary Beneath the Waves, CrAu (req Re) 30, Touch, Moon, Room, which makes air on the bed of a large body of water within an existing enclosure with clear bounds (p. 122).

neighbours.name: Vindolanda Gate, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: A chamber five paces square, with a passage east and the gateway to the Northumbrian site in an alcove in the west wall. Six inches of water; silt and debris (p. 123).

neighbours.name: Kerlingarfjoll Valley Gate, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: A chamber five paces square, with a passage west and the gateway to the hidden Icelandic valley in an alcove in the east wall. Unlike the archways the magi of Vindolanda made, this gatestone is the capstone of a trilithon. Six inches of water; silt and debris (pp. 123-124).

neighbours.name: Library, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: Twelve paces by ten, with four lecterns, four writing desks and about forty books in untidy piles on tables, under an enchantment of preservation: 900 levels of spells and 360 levels of books, with Ealasaid's translation notes and lab notes. Six inches of water; silt and debris (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Latrine, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: Eight paces by six, with stone benches on the north and south walls whose holes open on the drainage that destroys inanimate matter. Six inches of water; silt and debris (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Bath, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: Its magic items still work and, though three centuries of water have widened the drain, the bath stays warm and clean. The flood first stood about three feet deep here, until the drains of bath and latrine drew it down to the room's lowest drainage point. Six inches of water; silt and debris (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Ealasaid's Private Chambers, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: Her sanctum marker hangs on the remains of the door. A rotten bed and clothes chest, a writing desk, and on the lectern her last lab text, close to finishing the calling ritual for the Obsidian Gate. Six inches of water; silt and debris (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Ealasaid's Lab, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: Wholly submerged, its equipment past saving. Clay and basalt tablets here, in cuneiform and hieroglyphics, are how she identified the names and natures of the gateways' spirits (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Sea Dome Temple, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: A round chamber thirty paces across, now open to the sea, with steps up to an altar. Its thick granite dome, enchanted to transparency, lies on the floor under four feet of sand, silt and sea life. Restored, the temple would give +5 to magical summoning rituals; spirits of the sea and secretive spirits such as Lucifugus (Hedge Magic p. 77) favor it greatly. A fresh-water spring feeds a fountain in the altar, which yields twelve pawns of Intellego vis at the winter solstice each year (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Exit Tunnel, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: The first way in, eight miles long, ending in a cave in a cliff (p. 124).

neighbours.name: Ealasaid's Gate, Sea Temple
neighbours.summary: A room of the Sea Temple sanctum.
neighbours.secrets: An archway wholly flooded and full of silt. Its gatestone joins Macomb's sanctum but is out of position and cannot be used (pp. 123-124).

neighbours.name: Kerlingarfjoll Valley
neighbours.summary: A valley shut in by glacier-topped mountains, 30 km southwest of the peak of the Hofsjokull glacier.

levels.name: First magical level
levels.notes:
Secrets
A ruined temple in the Egyptian style, one mile long and half a mile wide, warmer than below with the sun higher in the sky (p. 96).

levels.name: Top level
levels.notes:
Secrets
Printed as the third level of a two-tier regio. It covers only the temple complex and walkway, whole here, in a Mediterranean climate, and the stars agree with Memphis in Egypt. The sacred architecture is bent on opening the gateway, so other magic that would gain from the aura does not; Infernal powers still take the usual -9 to Penetration (pp. 96-97).

neighbours.secrets:
Warm, green and fertile, about four miles long and a mile wide, with a small river through it; steam vents keep it warm and wrapped in mist (p. 96). Its mundane level is only fertile grassland.

A powerful ancient enchantment beats back all who try to climb in with rising wind and weather. It has a Penetration of +120 and also acts as a level 120 Aegis around the valley, but does not hinder the magic of creatures inside. A Wind of Mundane Silence strong enough for a level 120 spell overcomes it for Sun duration (p. 96).

Around 30 June the warding fails for about two and a half minutes, one diameter, at midnight, and the mundane level can then be found. Only Hetep knows this, having been present when Setna made the ward (p. 96).

The upper levels can be reached only with magic. A Perception + Second Sight roll of 15+ moves a character between levels, and spells for that must penetrate a Magic Resistance of 30 (p. 96).

neighbours.name: Temple of Thoth, Kerlingarfjoll
neighbours.summary: An Egyptian temple at the top of the valley's regio.
neighbours.secrets:
A paved road runs about a hundred paces to the entrance, under five trilithons with enchanted lintels. Four are useless, their partners destroyed; the one farthest from the temple leads to Ealasaid's Lundy sanctum, and once stood in a cave near Carnac (p. 96).

Within stands the Obsidian Gateway, a solid block shaped into an arch eight paces wide, sixteen high and a meter thick. The Thothian priests found it, and it joins its twin in the Obsidian Temple. Hieroglyphics on the walls tell of Setna's journey here, the raising of the temple, and his passage through the gate into the presence of Thoth (p. 96).

Any Gifted person who sees the Gate longs to go through. The first time a magus touches it he falls in a fit and sees Damhan-Allaidh as he was in 681, shadow twisted and eyes darkened, stepping through after a ritual; a dark wave then runs from the gate, warping the hieroglyphics and wall images into demonic shapes; then the Order falls to diabolism, cunning folk burn, and crusaders put books and scholars to the torch and sword. It ends in a wordless plea for help. A magus who offers help rolls once on the Good Effects table (ArM4 p. 182), one who refuses on the Bad Effects table; either way he gains only one Twilight point (p. 97).

Call of the Obsidian Serpent, ReVi 40 ritual (R: Spec, D: Spec, T: Ind), does not truly summon the daemon of the gate but draws its attention and asks it to come. It works only in this temple, on or around the last day of June; Ealasaid's notes give the date with Int + Artes Liberales 9+. It takes two hours, four from text, and must end at midday, timed by a shaft of light. The leader anoints the gate and declares his intent to summon its spirit, extols the spirit, chants the sacred words from Ealasaid's grimoire, and commands it to open as the light strikes the gateway's radial point. The oil takes eight pawns of Vim or Rego vis, serves as the ritual's vis, and takes a day in a lab. With The Mysteries, casting from text may need Theurgy 8; without Theurgy the spell must be learned and mastered. The gate then stays open while the caster concentrates (p. 97).

neighbours.name: Cadell and Enan
neighbours.summary: Two earth spirits at Glyder Fawr.
neighbours.secrets:
Two earth elementals left from those Macomb's apprentice called. Cadell is eager for a fight but will not strike unprovoked. Enan is more thoughtful and tries to talk a party into leaving. Both are good-natured and hold back from lethal force unless seriously threatened. Magi who convince them they belong to Vindolanda are welcomed and told of the battle with Damhan-Allaidh (p. 96).

If the magi want the site back, Enan raises the rent: the original deal with Vindolanda was one pawn each a year. They open at over six hundred pawns (one a year each), can be talked down to around sixty over the next decade, and for a suitable consideration may restore the site as well (p. 96). The book prints no statistics for them.

neighbours.name: The Trolls of Snaefellsnes
neighbours.summary: Trolls fill the Snaefellsnes peninsula, and to them a new household is prey.

stages.title: Stolen sheep
stages.clues: Sheep and the like go missing around the farms.
stages.ignored: With no reprisal the trolls grow bolder.

stages.title: Bolder attacks
stages.clues: The thefts turn into attacks on the covenant's interests.

neighbours.secrets: They come slowly into the saga, and only grow bolder if no reprisal follows (p. 89). Their statistics are on p. 30.

neighbours.name: The Hidden Revels
neighbours.summary: The dead of a Roman fort in Northumberland are said to beg for mercy every night.

details.antagonist: Ammon, Master of the Hidden Revels

stages.title: The first visit
stages.clues: Ammon and his minions; ideally the magi are forced to retreat.
stages.ignored: Ammon lets them go, with insults to bring them back (p. 94).

stages.title: Preparation
stages.clues: The magi research spells or invest items for the return (p. 93).

stages.title: The return
stages.clues: Spells must penetrate Might 40 to reach the top level, and the gatestones are under tons of rubble (pp. 93-94).
stages.stopped: With the infernal creatures gone, Christian burial for all the victims can destroy the regio, and a magical regio (+2, +4) forms within a decade (p. 94).

neighbours.secrets: The magi are best served by going before Brighde's Gauntlet, whose timing the storyguide may shift to suit (pp. 92-93).

neighbours.name: Burnham's Bargain
neighbours.summary: Burnham has a vis right in Northumberland it would like to exchange with a young covenant.
neighbours.secrets: Burnham holds the harvesting rights to Old Vindolanda and will maneuver the next naive young covenant into taking them (p. 93).

neighbours.name: Stad
neighbours.summary: The estate of the godi Thord Sturluson.
neighbours.secrets: Thord feasts the foreign magi here, and here Blund Thorgilsson's thirty horsemen ride in to summon them (p. 98).

neighbours.name: Blund's Farmstead
neighbours.summary: A rich farm on the north coast of Snaefellsnes, with several tenancies and its own church.
neighbours.secrets:
About 13 miles east of Thorsnes (p. 99). Every fertile woman and beast of the household is miscarrying. A Per + Second Sight roll of 9+ shows a great spirit cat falling on the swarms of flies that come over the rise, and Intellego Vim also finds them: Hlokk, Una's sickly house cat, is fighting them off.

The cause lies at the mud pits about 2 miles south.

neighbours.name: Blund's Mud Pits
neighbours.summary: A field of boiling mud pits on Snaefellsnes that the farmers shun.
neighbours.secrets:
Six pits in an exact circle, in a Magic aura of +4, about 2 miles south of Blund's farm; Per + Awareness 6+ spots something just under each surface. In each lies a white egg of Size +0, laid in the 3rd Century, of Pan Caudarax's brood. Blund and his people have no idea (pp. 98, 100).

In the middle stands a nidstong, a pole with a horse's head, whose runes promise loss to a killer of children. It is Einar Gamlisson's. Each day it stands there is a chance the curse takes the eggs; destroying it ends the effect (p. 101; p. 59). The pole is an Arcane Connection to Einar, but a broken one fades within twelve weeks. No Intellego reaches him in Glasvellir.

The disease spirits gather here, trying to get into the eggs, and vanish if the curse is broken. One egg is discoloured and its pit stinks of rot: the infant in it is dead, and spirits rise from it and fly down the valley to Blund's farm. Its shell holds 4 pawns of Terram and the body 3 of Animal, 3 of Vim and 3 of Ignem; the egg has no Magic Resistance and Soak +5 (pp. 100-101).

Guarding the site needs a mundane cover: hut-men from among the covenfolk, which Blund as landowner and the farmers' hreppur must accept, though the land can hardly feed them. Sulfur gathering might pass. The galdramen hreppur will not stand for anything a traveller could walk into; Intellego and regular visits are the easiest answer (p. 106).

neighbours.name: Dagverdara Farmstead
neighbours.summary: A farm of Thord Sturluson's on Snaefellsnes, under Snaefell.
neighbours.secrets: The farm nearest the tunnel, and Scartaris's foothold on the surface; about three miles separate the two (p. 89). Iain completes the purchase once Blund's affair is settled. With his money and De Panne's support it can employ up to thirty adults and their families, a huge household by Icelandic standards: the house must be greatly extended and perhaps a second one built. Iain links it to the Scartaris gateroom with the spare gatestones, and new Icelandic characters can enter the saga simply by coming here for work (p. 101). The story needs this farm later.

neighbours.name: Thord's Feast
neighbours.summary: A witchcraft suit draws the magi into Icelandic law when a cursed storbondi, Blund Thorgilsson, demands they lift the blight on his household, and the godi Thord Sturluson offers to stand behind them for a price (pp. 98-101).

stages.title: The feast at Stad
stages.clues: Iain asks Thord about buying or renting the farm nearest the Scartaris tunnel; Thord wants to know the magi first and invites them to dine. At mid-afternoon Blund rides in with thirty horsemen and summons them for witchcraft. Thord explains the law, offers his support if they become his thingmen, and offers the farm.
stages.ignored: If the magi will not join a godord, Iain does, and they count as his household. Owning the farm makes them residents, who must by law attach to a godord; that is no feudal bond, so it may pass under Hermetic Law, and as of 1220 the Peripheral Code has no ruling on it.

stages.title: The Thorsnes varthing
stages.clues: The case moves toward the Althing. Blund's man offers to drop it if the magi try to lift the curse, and Thord urges them to agree. Thord lends them Vifil as guide and interpreter; he is a galdraman sent to watch them, says so only if asked, and lacks the Gentle Gift, so they may well guess.
stages.ignored: If they refuse, the case goes to the Althing (see Meet the Dragon).

stages.title: Blund's farmstead
stages.clues: Women and beasts miscarry; Una's cat Hlokk sleeps and hardly eats. Second Sight or Intellego Vim reveals the fly spirits and the cat that hunts them.

stages.title: The Dragon's Nest
stages.clues: The spirits lead to six mud pits, six eggs, and a nidstong.
stages.stopped: Throwing down the nidstong ends the curse. Vifil says the rest is the hreppur's business: Blund should hear only that it is over, and being used to magicians' secrecy he will not press. Vifil tells them about Pan Caudarax, fears his reaction, and urges them to the hreppur meeting just after the Althing.
stages.turned: Magi who think of breaking the eggs bring Vifil out of hiding to explain why not.

stages.title: The covenant farmstead
stages.clues: With Blund satisfied Iain buys Dagverdara.

neighbours.secrets:
Blund wrongly took vengeance on a local witch, so the regional leader of the galdramen hreppur blacklisted him. He hopes to force the newcomers to help, and Thord hopes his suit brings them under his influence.

The curse is not aimed at Blund at all. Einar Gamlisson laid it on Pan Caudarax's eggs, laid in the 3rd Century, and the farm is merely near them. Einar has good reason to hate the eggs' father.

How Blund knows: the magi landed on Snaefellsnes with no known ship just as a demon beast ran wild, Brighde/Hetep's transformation had many witnesses, and Icelanders with Second Sight or Magical Sensitivity soon notice a Parma and a Gift. Rumour goes from farm to farm, and magi outside the hreppur are easy targets (p. 98).

neighbours.name: Hekla Lair
neighbours.summary: Wide tunnels at the foot of the Hekla volcano, in air hot, dry and sulfurous.
neighbours.secrets: Pan Caudarax's Icelandic lair, a Magic aura of +9. A river of lava comes from the far end of a vast cavern and flows down both sides into tunnels flanking the entrance. The dragon sleeps as a lindorm on a bed of pure white sand at the centre, in a red glow, with dozens of fire spirits darting into the lava (p. 105).

neighbours.name: Silver Spring of Snaefell
neighbours.summary: A hot spring on the north face of Snaefell.
neighbours.secrets: On the night of the winter solstice it runs with a silvery liquid usable as Vim vis. With the Ice Crystal Cave it is the hreppur's reward for a settlement with Pan Caudarax. The book recommends the two together give 3 pawns per magus per year; the storyguide sets the figure (p. 106).

neighbours.name: Ice Crystal Cave
neighbours.summary: An icy cave high on Snaefell.
neighbours.secrets: Through the summer it washes out odd ice crystals that do not melt until the summer solstice; gathered, they serve as Rego vis (p. 106). Shared yield with the Silver Spring of Snaefell.

neighbours.name: Meet the Dragon
neighbours.summary: The hreppur of Iceland's magicians calls the magi to Eldborg, and the dragon Pan Caudarax wants the priests of Hermes at his lair at the autumnal equinox to answer for the attack on his nest (pp. 102-106).

stages.title: The Althing
stages.clues: Vifil invites the magi to the hreppur, with the Althing as cover for the journey; they can see the market, the games and the procedure (p. 35).
stages.ignored: If they refused Blund or failed, they are at the Althing for the suit. Vifil has quietly found the cause; witchcraft cases embarrass the hreppur, so he helps Thord settle by offering to lift a curse that is already gone. Blund wants up to sixty ells of homespun for his delay and cost. Vifil then invites the magi anyway.

stages.title: The hreppur at Eldborg
stages.clues: Vifil translates. The rules on magical services, on owning vis (ond to Norsemen) and on discretion are read (p. 28). Bard Snaefellsass, who speaks for giants and greater spirits and mediates for them, delivers the dragon's message, and watches the newcomers on 'his' land without much interest. Biorn offers rights to a couple of vis sources for appeasing the dragon.
stages.ignored: Magi who helped no one are summoned anyway, from his long history with Latin magi and his curiosity; Vifil, having found the nidstong alone, goes too and tells the dragon they refused.
stages.stopped: Magi who will not go are told plainly they cannot stay in Iceland: he commands volcanoes across the land, and Scartaris sits on one.

stages.title: Hekla Lair
stages.clues: He greets them in archaic Latin, as priests of Hermes the Thrice Blessed, hears how the curse was found, and asks why he should not drive the human population into the sea.
stages.stopped: He settles for protection and then fostering of his remaining children, Hermetic training included: he will Transform them into human newborns when they hatch in twenty years, and the magi raise and teach them. He also offers a long hundred (120 pawns) of vis for the body of the magician responsible.

stages.title: Settlement
stages.clues: The hreppur grants the Silver Spring and the Ice Crystal Cave; if Vifil found the nidstong he takes an equal share. He also tells them of Odadahraun, whose vis is for anyone brave enough (p. 14). The nest is now theirs to guard (see Blund's Mud Pits).

neighbours.secrets:
One unborn dragon is dead and Pan Caudarax is sure to want revenge; the task is to keep it to the guilty. Had the hreppur known the truth of Blund's curse it would have acted at once, but it let him suffer because he had killed one of its own (p. 105).

The hreppur's authority is loose, with no oath or ceremony. Its agreement with the godar protects members from unwarranted suits, if they keep its laws; Eldborg and the pathway tax are voluntary. The Order of Hermes draws no objection from Biorn; the Order of Odin means nothing to anyone here (p. 105).

Einar cannot be traced for now: he is in Glasvellir, and no galdraman knows who attacked the nest. The nearest clue is the ship Pan Caudarax destroyed five years ago, on which many Icelanders lost kin, none known as magicians (p. 106).

Dragon magi. The Oath allows Hermetic training only for apprentices who will join the Order, and nothing forbids a non-human, though many would be vexed. The magi can agree: the dragons hatch in about 20 years, become human babies, start training five years later, and after 15 years' apprenticeship have no reason not to swear; the Order may debate it, but with no Oath broken a March is unlikely. They can agree and renegotiate or refuse in 25 years, when they may stand a chance against him. Or they can refuse now and be eaten (p. 106).

neighbours.name: The Mate of Pan Caudarax
neighbours.summary: Story seed (p. 106): a true Scandinavian lindorm, serpent bodied, small limbed and venomous of bite, may swim to Iceland to see how her brood fares under their father's guidance. Those fostering the young may not know who she is.

neighbours.name: The Troll Caves of Snaefell
neighbours.summary: A cave reaching far back into the mountains near Snaefell, shunned by men.
neighbours.secrets: Kollbjorn's trolls hold this cave system; its head is a night's shelter on the winter road to Bard. The trolls and the mountain giants keep a truce that begins only on the Longest Night. Passages twist and divide, some very narrow, some widened, and toward midday one section runs through a glacier in faint blue light (pp. 108-109).

neighbours.name: The Singing Cave
neighbours.summary: A deep, nearly closed valley among five mountains on Snaefellsnes, known by its echoes.
neighbours.secrets: Songhellir in Norse. It looks like a cavern, but its roof is open and the winter sun comes down to a floor nearly three hundred paces across; every voice echoes perfectly. Bard holds his midwinter feast here (p. 109). No aura is printed.

neighbours.name: Skjalfandi
neighbours.summary: An island near Husavik, home of a hermit known for his holiness and his care of hurt animals.
neighbours.secrets: Reached by a borrowed boat. It lies in a Divine aura, of no printed strength (pp. 111-112). In the ashes of the hermit's fire lies the silver arrowhead, scratched with a runic curse to drain power from a spirit; he burnt the arrow as soon as he drew it.

neighbours.name: Trolls of the Western Quarter
neighbours.summary: Trolls of Snaefellsnes, the thickest concentration in Iceland (p. 125), who steal much-needed livestock (p. 107).
neighbours.secrets: Led by Kollbjorn, with his mother Skrukka and the henchmen Gapi and Gljufra-Geir. Trolls' law forbids stealing from or killing a relative (p. 108).

neighbours.name: The Scottish Giants
neighbours.summary: A dozen or so brutish giants from Scotland, stranded in Iceland and barely tolerated by its giants, who think them barbarians.
neighbours.secrets:
Five appear at Bard's feast: Suil Aon (sool-oon, One-Eye), Creagcas (kreg kos, Rock-Foot), Beinn (beyn, Mountain), Sruth Dubh (sroo-doo, Black Tide) and their leader Geamhradh Grian (gev-ra grean, Winter Sun). They speak Pictish, Jotunn and Gaelic. Use the giants' statistics of p. 31; none has magical abilities.

Damhan-Allaidh laid a geas on the clan after Victor took the Carnac gateway, seeking another road to the temple: they cannot leave Iceland until they have visited the Temple of Thoth in the Kerlingarfjoll valley. They have found the valley but not the way in. Bard wants them gone and knows nothing of it (p. 111).

Telling them frees Iceland of them but may hand Damhan-Allaidh vital secrets. One answer: set the Kerlingarfjoll gatestone outside the covenant and walk them through briefly, so the geas is met and they still cannot find the way in. Freed, they go home and refuse him further service; otherwise he forces them to one last service (pp. 111, 125).

neighbours.name: Bard's Daughters
neighbours.summary: The nine golden-haired daughters of Bard Snaefellsass, all healers.
neighbours.secrets: Giantesses. By his first wife: Helga, Thordis and Solrun. By his second: Ragnhild, Flaumgerd, Thora, Thorkild, Geirrid and Mjoll. Some, Helga among them, have great magic, others less; all have the Jotunn Affinity with Frost and the Healer talent. A child of one and a human is likely to be a trollson (p. 112).

neighbours.name: Thorkel's Sons
neighbours.summary: Six giants of the clan of Hrym, sons of Thorkel and much like him: Red-Cloak, Solvi, Svadi, Ox-Thorir, Asvald and Skeggi.
neighbours.secrets: All share his temper, though Ox-Thorir finds humans intriguing and wants to know more. Red-Cloak, the eldest, torments Helga, Bard's daughter, because he is drawn to her (p. 113).

neighbours.name: Feast of Thanks
neighbours.summary: Bard Snaefellsass, a giant and the people of Snaefell's half-remembered protector, invites the characters to his midwinter feast in thanks for appeasing Pan Caudarax, and sets them among Iceland's supernatural powers (pp. 107-112). Best where the covenant already has trouble with trolls.

details.antagonist: The Scottish giants, and the rivalries around Bard's table

stages.title: The invitation
stages.clues: At dawn a grog sees a huge gray dog (Size +0) with folded ears and a short nose, which leads him into a ravine, passes behind a boulder, and comes out as a man over eight feet tall. Bard asks them to his midwinter feast and whistles the dog away.
stages.ignored: If they refuse he seems hurt, and sends Solrun anyway, trusting to her charm.

stages.title: Solrun
stages.clues: A month or so before midwinter a woman seeks shelter from a storm of several days and wins the covenfolk with tales of the Old Gods, which may offend the devout. Deep snow keeps her on. On the morning before the solstice she asks for the magi by name, says she has come to take them to Bard, and calls herself his servant, not his daughter.

stages.title: The journey
stages.clues: Clear, dark weather; they need lights, as the sun barely rises at noon. She leads them through the mountains at a cost of a fatigue level by day's end, to a cave. She warns them off the tunnels, since the truce between trolls and giants does not begin until the Longest Night, and her father is godi of the region's giants.

stages.title: Meeting the troll-king
stages.clues: In the night one man, best a grog with an eye for Solrun, sees her cloak go into the tunnel. It is Skrukka's illusion; companions are split up by more of the same. His torch gutters, and Kollbjorn lurches out of the dark, calling for Bravery rolls.
stages.ignored: Kollbjorn wrests away any weapon, declares his life forfeit and offers whatever deal suits the saga. Skrukka seals it with a Curse of fitting Flaws, lifted once he keeps his side (see The Troll-Bride).

stages.title: The Singing Cave
stages.clues: Solrun leaves them in the glacier passage. Bard greets them; seven of his daughters bring mead. His brother Thorkel comes from the shadows, shrinking with each stride to a mere nine feet, sneering at humans.

stages.title: The feast
stages.clues: About two dozen guests, four of them trolls, the giants shrunk to Size +3 or less. Roast horse, illegal heathen fare in Iceland, and two fermented sharks. Bard toasts Freyr, Njordur and the Almighty God, meaning Thor. Thordis, beside the party's leader, toasts the guests; Thorkel recites his ancestors back to Kari son of Ymir; a troll toasts Kollbjorn. At least one character must toast, or the air chills, and Int + Etiquette 6+ (Icelanders 3+) warns against toasting the host. Bard answers questions freely.

stages.title: Guests from afar
stages.clues: Five thin, black-haired giants shout their way in, squabbling in Pictish over a sack of sheep, and call the characters dessert. Thorkel's party chuckles. Their leader says he will not feast with animals. Bard cannot command them without risking the rest of the clan, and advises a show of strength.
stages.ignored: Characters who make no impression are treated poorly.
stages.stopped: Size +6 by Bard's Transform (Ease Factor 31 + Magic Resistance, stress die + 37, once per willing character), or Str + Intimidation 9+, flashy magic at any size, boasts on Com + Guile or Storytelling 9+, or beating one fairly, even to death, earns their respect and a seat beside them.

stages.title: Matters of trust
stages.clues: Bard draws the giants to talk of their geas. They mention an immense eagle on a Northern Quarter shore with a lance-sized arrow in its breast. Bard turns grave and begs the characters to investigate.

stages.title: The Second Guardian
stages.clues: The trail runs from the cove to Husavik, its priest, and the hermit of Skjalfandi, who tends a slowly failing eagle.
stages.stopped: The eagle is Vindsvall, forced into solid shape by the arrow. Tended by a man of True Faith in a Divine aura he regains no Might, and Int + Magic Theory 12+ shows the Divine is killing him; the hermit blames the witchery on the arrowhead. He recovers if the hermit, who has an uncanny sense for lies, can be persuaded to stop, or if fed Animal, Auram, Creo or Vim vis. Out of the Dominion he calls his landvaettir, flocks of birds feed him Might, and he swells to his true form and flies off. A hermit who sees it swears it was an angel (p. 112).

neighbours.secrets: Bard believes Iceland's guardians are under attack. The first was Pan Caudarax; the second is Vindsvall, now found shot; the third has been blunted by the Dominion; the fourth is himself (p. 111). He makes no claim to be more than a man who pays his debts, though Int + Area Lore 8+ ties his name to the spirit locals thank when disaster passes.

neighbours.name: The Troll-Bride
neighbours.summary: Story seed (p. 108): Kollbjorn's price for the trespasser's life is marriage to his daughter Drit.
neighbours.secrets: Skrukka lays Curses of Lost Love and Short Attention Span on the groom, so he will come to the wedding to be rid of them. The feast is frightening: horse and human flesh, violent games, a rock-catching game for the humans. Skrukka performs the rite and the trolls drink themselves senseless, meaning to eat the guests but not the groom; Solrun comes by night to get them out. Kollbjorn's clan gives chase until several trolls are dead. A troll-chief for a father-in-law may in time bring peace between covenant and trolls, since their law protects kin, though Skrukka will likely oppose it.

neighbours.name: Iceland's Enemy
neighbours.summary: Story seed (p. 112): is anything truly hunting Iceland's guardians?
neighbours.secrets: The book leaves it deliberately open whether a systematic threat exists: Einar Gamlisson may work alone, or someone unknown may be using him.

neighbours.name: The Gray Bull
neighbours.summary: Story seed (p. 112): Bard, fearing a supernatural attack, perhaps by Damhan-Allaidh himself, asks the characters to 'rescue' Iceland's third guardian from the Dominion's grip.
neighbours.secrets: The Bishop of Skalholt owns the bull and will not part with it, for its many fine calves have made him prosperous, so a raid may be needed. Let loose on pasture free of the Dominion it casts off its tameness and over a matter of weeks, faster in a magical aura, grows dramatically; it lets no human near, and takes up Iceland's defence again.

neighbours.name: Glasvellir
neighbours.summary: The Glittering Plains, an underworld spoken of in old tales.

levels.name: The Glittering Plains
levels.notes:
Secrets
A magical regio of level 8 with no lower levels, under the glacier in Snaefell's central crater. On or around the last day of June at midday the shadow of Scartaris peak falls on the caldera glacier, the ice breaks, and a 2,800-foot shaft opens until the third sunset after. No roll is needed to enter. Cut off from the mundane realm: Leap of Homecoming and any spell or item for communication fail. The only sure ways home are the way in and the Obsidian Gate (pp. 115-116).

neighbours.secrets:
The road (pp. 115-116): the glacier has a Magic aura of +3 and the shaft +4, which cannot be found at other times. A steep tunnel runs east by southeast for a day and a half to a fork. The eastern way goes on two days, then rises to a dead end a day later, by which time the entrance has sealed. The western way goes a day and meets a hole in the wall jetting hot, drinkable water, from a fast river beyond a few feet of granite; the aura is +5 here, and the stream shows the road. Then two days southwest, level, past side tunnels that all fail, and a near-vertical crack of a stair for two and a half days, the stream a torrent, into a cavern with a barely visible roof and an aura of +8.

Other tunnels lead out, none known to go anywhere, and digging by spell is as haphazard.

Gudmund's realm has plains of golden barley and lush growth that glow softly. The arrival bank is about 200 yards wide under the cavern wall; the river is nearly 300 yards across and far too fast to swim, though it has cooled. Those swept off and able to stay afloat (Str + Swim) reach Geirrod's bank. A day downstream a bridge of what seems solid gold crosses it, or magic and ropes will serve. On the far side the barley stands eight feet tall, goats match cows, and cows match elephants (p. 116).

Small families of twelve-foot giants herd and reap along the river and feed the city far to the southeast, where about three hundred families live in luxury under Gudmund. Most can shapeshift and have no other magic (p. 116).

Gudmund's wonders (p. 117): a many-coloured waterfall and a cave of perfect echoes; a hall being built of gold studded with gems, from nuggets the river leaves on its banks; the hunt for immense boar in thick forest; a spring on a rocky hillock that tastes of the finest honey-mead, a draft of it holding 3 pawns of Creo vis and granting the Free Expression virtue for a day; the village of humans; and a day-long feast with the court's illusions.

neighbours.name: The Humans of Glasvellir
neighbours.summary: A village descended from people who strayed into Glasvellir centuries ago.
neighbours.secrets: They live in peace with its giants, speak West Norse and keep the heathen Norse gods. Einar Gamlisson settled here and started a new family. Geirrod's people raided the village lately and took several children as slaves or meat, Einar's among them; questions are referred to Gudmund (p. 117).

neighbours.name: Gudmund's People
neighbours.summary: The fair folk of Glasvellir, more courtiers than warriors.
neighbours.secrets: Size +3, bigger than trolls, far smaller than giants proper. They usually have no magic but Shapechange in a handful of forms. About one in twenty is magically powerful, with the full range of trollsynir abilities and often Jotunn Affinities; these are usually his men-at-arms. The court has experts in illusion. His twelve sons attend him, all in red like their father (pp. 116, 119).

neighbours.name: Geirrodargard
neighbours.summary: The land beyond the icy Hemra River on the north of the Glittering Plains.
neighbours.secrets:
The sky seems dark red, thin mist lies on black soil and blasted plants, and packs of immense dogs roam so that almost nothing lives outside the city. There is one ford over the Hemra, about five miles from the city (p. 117).

The obsidian-walled city is over five miles across, its walls three hundred feet high. Over two thousand trolls live there, with about five hundred human slaves, in ruin and decay under smoke that cuts sight to under fifteen paces. Visitors must trick their way in (p. 118).

One thing stands whole, hidden at the centre: a ziggurat over five hundred feet high, seemingly cut from a single block of obsidian, three golden winged sphinxes guarding its triple stairs, its one chamber at the summit behind an iron door. Its residents never go near it and have forgotten what it was (pp. 118, 130).

The Hemra ford is where Einar stands with the Norns (p. 118).

neighbours.name: Geirrod's People
neighbours.summary: The trolls of Geirrodargard, shorter than Gudmund's folk, twisted and ugly, as mean and petty as any troll.
neighbours.secrets: Physically identical to trolls, kin to those the characters know. Many have a Jotunn Affinity with Fire and many of the females the Gift of the Magic Arts (p. 119). Their human slaves, about five hundred, have been hearing the Aesir religion from Einar (p. 127).

neighbours.name: The Norn Landvaettir
neighbours.summary: Spirits of fate called up by orlog-galdor, seen as countless shadowy shapes about a lady.
neighbours.secrets: Einar stands high among them, and their lady will help him. They can pass the characters off as human slaves and hide them from Second Sight. Attacking Einar enrages the lady and her court (p. 118).

neighbours.name: The Glittering Plains
neighbours.summary: Two years before the dragon eggs hatch, a rumour of a horde of dragons sets the Snaefellsnes farmers against the nest, and the man behind it can at last be followed (pp. 114-119).

stages.title: A plot is hatching
stages.clues: Around mid-July the peddler Kar Liefsson tells of dragons coming to Snaefellsnes, and of a tall wooden device at Blund's farm with ropes, pulleys and a huge iron-tipped stake pointing down: a pile driver to skewer the infants in their shells. Covenfolk who visit the nest may bring the news instead.

stages.title: Blund's farm
stages.clues: Blund has left with labourers and householders. Una says one Einar Gamlisson stayed a night, warned them, and told Blund to go and look at the pits himself.

stages.title: The pile driver
stages.clues: Unless the magi are very swift, the driver stands over the first pit and the stake has just cracked the shell; one more blow will skewer the wounded infant. Guards may delay them. Mob rule should not be underrated.
stages.ignored: Blund has few days left if he harms one of the brood.
stages.stopped: Talk or force stops Blund, ideally without telling too much, and the dragonet is calmed and tended.

stages.title: Einar's journey
stages.clues: A man alone is remarked on. He rode west toward Snaefell, to his brother Thorodd's farm. The crater shows no entrance; Bard or Pan Caudarax can say it opens three days a year, so the magi wait a year.

stages.title: A long way down
stages.clues: The shaft, the tunnels and the river (see Glasvellir).

stages.title: Seven days with Gudmund
stages.clues: Asked about Einar, Gudmund looks troubled and says to ask tomorrow, for six days, showing a new wonder each day. On the seventh he explains: he hoped they would stay. Einar came years ago in sorrow and settled in the human village, and was last seen going into Geirrod's realm. Gudmund means to avenge the raid in his own time, and thinks anyone following Einar throws his life away. He had not mentioned Geirrod, with whom his people are at open odds; the raid looks like a prelude to battle.

stages.title: Einar's preparations
stages.clues: On the road to the Hemra ford they find Einar bargaining with a landvaettir lady amid shadowy shapes, using orlog-galdor to learn of his children and to cloud the trolls' sight.
stages.ignored: Attacking him brings the lady's anger on the players.
stages.turned: They can talk instead (see this story's secrets).

stages.title: Rescue
stages.clues: Geirrod's feast to rally his people against Gudmund will have the captured children roasted as its centrepiece. There are about three days. The storyguide fills in the rescue. The Norns can pass the characters as slaves; Veil of Invisibility with a Group version of Seven League Stride makes it trivially easy.
stages.ignored: Einar dies in the attempt.
stages.stopped: The rescue humiliates Geirrod, wins great favour with Gudmund, and makes Einar more than willing to settle with Pan Caudarax.

neighbours.secrets:
The galdraman Einar Gamlisson stirs up the farmers and is gone before the magi come. Pan Caudarax killed his first wife and their two children, and he has killed at least one of the dragon's. His honour is partly satisfied, so terms are possible: a settlement at the hreppur with compensation each way, even each fostering the other's child (p. 118).

What matters to him now is his living children, whom Geirrod's people took. Without the characters' help he dies trying to save them (p. 119).

neighbours.name: Brighde's Gauntlet
neighbours.summary: About twenty years into the saga Brighde's training ends: Victor leaves her body and she is set down alone in a remote part of Flanders for her Gauntlet, to cast out the demon within her (pp. 120-124).

stages.title: Council meeting
stages.clues: Victor calls a dreamscape council for the following spring and explains the plan. Brighde, raised Tytalus and fighting the demon alone under his eye for three years, is sure of herself. She has made a mirror showing whatever she sees, even under Hetep, who does not know of it, and it goes to the players. Other demons fall outside the Gauntlet, so they may help her against those.

stages.title: The gauntlet
stages.clues: Hetep takes her and heads west. He meets the demonic crow Whisper (p. 83), who tells him Damhan-Allaidh's last location in a tongue Brighde cannot understand, and resolves to take his old pawn as a host. The mirror lets the players see he is making for Old Vindolanda. If she tries the Leap he blocks her, and that fight does not end before Damhan-Allaidh is found.

stages.title: Old Vindolanda
stages.clues: See p. 93. Hetep has dug up the Lundy Island gatestone and is freeing Damhan-Allaidh; his minion Ammon guards the gateway and must be beaten.

stages.title: Damhan-Allaidh's tomb
stages.clues: Hetep fills the chamber with air by Creo Auram, digs the body from the rubble, abandons Brighde, possesses his ally and pours in Infernal Might. Within a few rounds Damhan-Allaidh wakes and tries to kill her before she can Leap.
stages.stopped: Quick players may save her. A player Brighde may fight it out as a dreamscape hunt for the Leap's hidden trigger, and should get away at the last moment unless very slow. A non-player Brighde may die here.

stages.title: Victor's farewell
stages.clues: Brighde is held in the lab ward with no demon in it, and only Victor's end frees her. He gives what last advice he can and wishes his filia well.
stages.ignored: If Brighde dies he stays in his body, and will not possess anyone again, willing or not, having grown uneasy at the sin of it. Trapped in ice, he speaks through Creo Mentem and uses his Morphean Landscape to hold meetings and teach them for the final conflict.

neighbours.secrets:
Victor's plan. Demonic deceit defeats magic, but demons can be fooled, and only Hetep knows where Damhan-Allaidh lies, whom Victor means to see destroyed. For one season a year he has taught her the Arts, and for the other three how to fight the demon he locked in her. On leaving her he goes back to his own body, still preserved in his Scartaris lab behind a ward that falls only at his death. Brighde lets Hetep seem to win; the player magi follow to the lair; she Leaps home by a waiting spell into the restored ward; Hetep is held in Victor's body, and Victor destroys it, holding the spirit for the Thothian Watchers (p. 84). That is his death and his choice, and it frees Brighde.

Hetep's plan. He has learnt to break free of her and can block the Leap. He bides his time; with Victor gone he means to take another host, kill her and escape.

If Brighde is a player character whose player refuses, Hetep escapes into one of the covenfolk and is pursued instead (p. 121).

The story should end with Damhan-Allaidh and Hetep escaping. If Victor knew of Hetep's threat to the Magic Realm he would destroy himself at once, but nobody knows of it yet (p. 122).

neighbours.name: Spider Through Mist
neighbours.summary: Damhan-Allaidh, possessed by Hetep, breaks into the Kerlingarfjoll valley and tries to pass the Obsidian Gateway; if he does, the sacred stelae are corrupted (pp. 125-126). Best about four years before the players can finish the Obsidian Gate ritual.

stages.title: Foreshadowing
stages.clues: Near the end of June, Per + Premonitions 6+ warns of danger; failing their own insight, players roll Intelligence 6+ to recall that the Gate may be opened and the Glasvellir tunnels reached about now. Guards might go to the valley and the Snaefell caldera.

stages.title: The assault
stages.clues: At midnight on the day the ritual can be performed he and his allies enter the mundane level of the valley, by a gap only Hetep knows. Then the tear, which gives guards time to warn Scartaris.
stages.ignored: If the magi take more than ten minutes, the first giant through tries to smash the trilithon linked to the covenant.
stages.stopped: With the Scottish giants the fight is very hard, and if they are ahead in a close battle they may let the characters retreat. If he is losing or falls, Hetep casts Leap of Homecoming; the giants then offer an honourable truce. Other allies panic, cannot leave the regio level, and can be dealt with at leisure.

stages.title: Damhan-Allaidh succeeds
stages.clues: He opens the Gate, steps through and smashes it at once, drives off its guardian spirit Setna, and Hetep finishes corrupting the stelae (his Corrupt Knowledge power, p. 137). He stays, still possessed, to guard them.
stages.ignored: Run Into the Gateway's first section.

stages.title: Damhan-Allaidh fails
stages.clues: He flees to Snaefell and the Glasvellir tunnels, claims Geirrod's protection and tries the Obsidian Temple from outside. Followers past the city gates face Geirrod and his troll army, until he betrays Geirrod.
stages.ignored: Run Into the Gateway's second section.

neighbours.secrets:
His allies depend on the storyguide and on Feast of Thanks: the Scottish giants are forced to serve unless their geas was met, in which case they have gone home and refuse him. Side stories may have the characters foil his search for allies.

Hetep knows a break in the ward, and a ritual like Tearing the Mystic Veil (Wizard's Grimoire Revised) that opens a tear wide enough for giants. It takes an hour to perform and ten minutes to widen, with a huge disturbance on both levels.

If the stelae fall, corruption spreads to all magical writing in the world, far slower than if Hetep did it directly, with much variation. An average summa turns in as many years as the experience points it holds (55 for level 10); a Tractatus or Liber Quaestionum in years equal to its Quality; an average Authority in over 365. Books written meanwhile are corrupt from the start (p. 126).

neighbours.name: The Spider Among the Trolls
neighbours.summary: Story seed (p. 125): trolls on Snaefellsnes, the thickest concentration in Iceland, are being gathered under one leader.
neighbours.secrets: Needing allies, Damhan-Allaidh tries to unite the Western Quarter's trolls, no easy task with so territorial and quarrelsome a people, and the characters live among them.

neighbours.name: Leiken and the Mara
neighbours.summary: Story seed (p. 125): old women ride the covenfolk through terrifying dreams, sapping their strength.
neighbours.secrets: The mara are evil landvaettir, witch-spirits, led by Leiken, among the most powerful of the yarthkin (p. 33), who has joined Damhan-Allaidh. After a few attacks Victor may be persuaded to let the characters fight them on their own terms in his Morphean Landscape. If he is dead, it is harder.

neighbours.name: The Obsidian Temple
neighbours.summary: Nothing is known of this place.
neighbours.secrets:
Where Thoth hid the first magical writings, reached from the summit chamber of the ziggurat in Geirrodargard or by the Obsidian Gateway. It is neither in the mundane world nor a regio, but a cut-off part of the Magic Realm with a +10 aura, in which magical abilities may break out in small ways; how strange is the storyguide's choice. There is no way on into the Realm: Setna warns those who try, and beyond the walls is only the Twilight Void, at the least an automatic temporary Twilight (p. 130).

Three golden sphinxes guard the entrance, then come seven gates: iron, bronze, wood, ivory, ebony, silver and gold. Each opens by ritual from cryptic instructions on it (pp. 130-132). The roll is the best Intelligence plus the two best of Magic Theory or equivalent, Occult Lore, Enigmatic Wisdom, Philosophiae and Artes Liberales, among all who can really contribute, plus the highest quality die anyone rolls; Mythic Intelligence adds 5 and Mythic Feats do not apply. A failure spends the base time. Each full 3 points above the difficulty halves the time.

Iron and Bronze, one week each, difficulty 18 and 21. Wood and Ivory, one month, 24 and 27. Ebony and Silver, one season, 30 and 33. Gold, one year, 36. The doors cannot be damaged and are beyond Hermetic magic (p. 132).

The Sanctum of the Stelae (p. 131): a black hemisphere 343 cubits (about 150 paces) across. The twin of the Obsidian Gateway stands at its centre, and before it a huge seated statue of Setna in gneiss, an ibis for Thoth at the back of his head; his spirit usually dwells in it. Around the wall stand seven emerald pillar stelae, seven cubits (about 3 paces) high, their hieroglyphics unknown. To a student Setna accepts they shift into his own tongue. They allow Arcane Experimentation (WGRE pp. 83-87) with no vis, lab or control rolls, the Research Lab Total at +10 for the aura; or they serve as a Quality 10 Authority on any magical Art or Knowledge. One student at a time, for no more than four seasons each.

neighbours.name: Into the Gateway
neighbours.summary: The magi finish Ealasaid's work on the Obsidian Gateway and must break into the Obsidian Temple to destroy the corrupted stelae, or defend them (pp. 127-132). Which half is played turns on the end of Spider Through Mist. It closes the saga.

stages.title: Corrupted: the wasteland
stages.clues: The spirit of the Gate sets them down at the edge of a corrupted waste in the Magic Realm, not at the Temple. Setna greets them warmly, begs their help and shows them Hetep's poison at work. He teaches Setna's Blade, tells of the other entrance at the ziggurat's summit, and gives directions to the Glittering Plains, knowing nothing of who lives there now. They may go back to Kerlingarfjoll to prepare.

stages.title: Corrupted: assault on Geirrodargard
stages.clues: With Einar and Gudmund, they sneak in as Gudmund besieges the city, and need only open the gates and hold them while the slaves' poison works. The fight at the gate should be hard.
stages.stopped: Geirrod orders his people to stop and sues for terms. Unless a Setna's Blade was made for him he lives, and he gives up Damhan-Allaidh's soulstone, frees the slaves and opens the ziggurat; Gudmund takes tribute in gold. Destroying the soulstone forces Hetep to Raise Corpse at once, binding him to the body so that he can possess no one; destroying the body lets the Thothian spirits take him.

stages.title: Corrupted: into the Obsidian Temple
stages.clues: Sphinxes and seven gates (easier with Geirrod beaten) lead to Damhan-Allaidh and Hetep. If Damhan-Allaidh still lives Hetep may try to possess magi and strong companions; resisted, he falls to the Thothian spirits.
stages.stopped: At the last the magi smash the emerald stelae to end the spread of the corruption.

stages.title: Uncorrupted: the sanctum
stages.clues: The Gate spirit takes them to the stelae sanctum. Setna greets them, knows only that Damhan-Allaidh is coming through the gates, and gives the Blade scroll. Investigation in Glasvellir shows what has passed. The sphinxes barred him, Geirrod would not help, so he bound Geirrod in magical iron, left snakes dripping venom on his faces to learn where the soulstone is, and made himself king of the trolls. He has since destroyed the three sphinxes, at great cost in trolls, and is at the ivory gate, the others left open.

stages.title: Uncorrupted: a web for the Spider
stages.clues: They may trap him in the sanctum as he opens the golden door. Setna conjures food and drink while they study the stelae.

stages.title: Uncorrupted: cutting the Spider's thread
stages.clues: Or they return by the Gate, which they may do at will, and go to Glasvellir, tell Einar and Gudmund, and open the gates during the siege. The strongest trolls are dead or maimed, so the city is lightly held. It should still be hard, since success ends Damhan-Allaidh and Hetep both.
stages.stopped: Gudmund frees his brother and leads the slaves to his realm, with a substantial tribute.
stages.turned: They may do both at once, some defending the sanctum and some striking from outside, or may have chased him into Glasvellir after the valley fight. End it dramatically.

neighbours.secrets:
If they succeed, Hetep is imprisoned and the Magic Realm saved. Victor, if alive, says goodbye and dispels his ward. With stelae uncorrupted the magi could win untold power and fame; the storyguide may consider which Hermetic Limits are only Hermetic and which are limits of Magic, and from there the saga is his (pp. 129-130).

Without Einar and Gudmund's support either assault is much harder. Einar has been teaching the Aesir religion to the human slaves and plans a rising, and they can poison the trolls wholesale when the gates open.

neighbours.name: Bergen
neighbours.summary: A Norwegian port with ships bound for Iceland.
neighbours.secrets: Hadrianus and his two filii took ship here in 1214 (Icelandic Wars p. 1). The ship of Flambeau magi in Land of Fire & Ice p. 70 sailed from here on a separate voyage in 1218. This is not the Bergen on Rügen.

neighbours.name: The Haunted Scottish Island
neighbours.summary: One of the Scottish isles, unnamed, which islanders say is haunted.
neighbours.secrets: The drowned body of Hadrianus came ashore here and his spirit walks the island. In 1224 a magus of Loch Leglean meets it and hears its broken story; having told it, the spirit rests (Icelandic Wars p. 2).

neighbours.name: Sinus Wodinis
neighbours.summary: A covenant of House Bjornaer on a frozen bay of Norway's southern coast, long out of touch with the Order. Its magi dislike strangers.
neighbours.secrets: The Mythic Seas pp. 62-63 prints it, and has it on a perpetually frozen bay. Crusaders may send to it for Bjornaer help; its magi may be allied with Norse wizards, and one may be a trollson (Icelandic Wars p. 9). That book places it on an island off the southeast coast; here that is only a rumour.

neighbours.name: The Southeastern Harbor
neighbours.summary: A bay on Iceland's southeastern quarter, where a ship can anchor.
neighbours.secrets: The armada's surviving ship drops anchor here, and if the Gray Bull is free it charges into the bay (Icelandic Wars p. 8).

neighbours.name: The Crusaders' Mystic Tower
neighbours.summary: A very remote part of Iceland's southeastern highlands, in a valley with mountains around it.
neighbours.secrets:
Once the crusade lands (or Bjornaer magi carry the materials ashore) a Hermes Portal is secretly set up here; a strong force comes through, conjures a Mystic Tower and casts an Aegis of the Hearth, and hunts Iceland's magicians from it (Icelandic Wars p. 9).

Julius's magi keep Gull's son here, alive through his External Soul, and cut him for vis (p. 11). Gull's hammer needs seven strikes to break the Aegis; if it falls, over a hundred giants cross the valley and the host tears the tower apart (p. 12).

neighbours.name: The Hermetic Crusaders
neighbours.summary: Magi of Houses Flambeau and Guernicus who want action against the Norse wizards.
neighbours.ruler: Julius of Flambeau and Lavinia of Guernicus

details.wants: Revenge for Hadrianus, and the end of the Order of Odin

neighbours.secrets:
Led by Julius and Lavinia, for idealism, glory or vis. With strong support the force is twelve powerful hoplites and twenty moderately powerful magi, mostly Flambeau, with Albinus and a hundred well-equipped grogs a ship beyond the crew. If support is undermined Albinus, six hoplites and five other magi stay home; if the hreppur was rebuffed, eight hoplites and ten other magi leave it, and Albinus turns against them (Icelandic Wars p. 7).

They carry spells for killing huge beasts and vis to pierce any resistance, but know nothing of spirits unless told (pp. 6, 8).

neighbours.name: The Magi Against the Crusade
neighbours.summary: Magi who say the Order of Odin is a myth, and are threatened for it by Flambeau and Guernicus magi as traitors.
neighbours.secrets: Older magi stand ready against a real threat and have no time for childish adventures. If the player characters argue well many powerful magi withdraw, and after the War Tribunal some pledge to take the matter to the Grand Tribunal (Icelandic Wars pp. 3-4).

neighbours.name: The Loch Leglean Tribunal
neighbours.summary: The Order's Tribunal in Scotland.
neighbours.secrets: One of its magi looks into the haunting of Hadrianus in 1224 (Icelandic Wars p. 2).

neighbours.name: The Icelandic Wars
neighbours.summary:
An outline of how the Order of Hermes might go to war with Iceland over a myth, written for the Toframanna Saga but with seeds for players on either side. Hermetic archmagi meet the guardians, the landvaettir and the giant clans; unless the player characters are as strong, they work by politics and tactics, guarding their own future and limiting the ruin. The book's aim is story, and storyguides should fit it to their own troupe and power level.

Three of the book's events carry years before the fleet sails; everything after that has none, and the outcome hangs on what the characters do. The conflict barely touches the mainland's mundane history, but could alter Iceland's: see Land of Fire & Ice p. 18.

details.antagonist: Archmagi Julius of Flambeau and Lavinia of Guernicus

stages.title: The Bergen Expedition
stages.clues: For over a century rumours of a Norse order and the loss of spring covenants in Scandinavia have fed the Order's fear; each search has found only weak hedge wizards. In 1214 Hadrianus hears of a great society of magicians on Iceland.
stages.ignored: The landvaettir watchers sense the ship's intent and tell Pan Caudarax, who burns it. Hadrianus's filii die; he kills a band of landvaettir, falls into Twilight on a botched spell and is drowned. His body drifts to a Scottish island.

stages.title: The Ghost Speaks
stages.clues: The covenant's redcap brings news of Hadrianus's ghost, and of whom it blames. Over the next couple of years magi start to say something must be done.
stages.ignored: A Loch Leglean magus meets the ghost, which blames the Order of Odin and then rests; a summoning for more sends it into Final Twilight. The Primus of Flambeau demands vengeance, Guernicus magi press their old case, and Julius and Lavinia start preparing.

stages.title: The War Tribunal
stages.clues: A few years after the ghost, letters reach every covenant of the northern Tribunals asking for help and for knowledge of Iceland. Lavinia then calls a special Tribunal at Durenmar, in the Rhine Tribunal, open to all with an interest.
stages.ignored: The Tribunal declares all Icelandic magicians enemies of the Order, their lives forfeit, in revenge for Hadrianus, and Lavinia rules that binding. Those who kept quiet will not be thanked by the winner.
stages.stopped: It cannot quite be stopped: the war party has the loudest voice, wanting a hedge-wizard hunt, glory or new vis. If the hreppur swears the Oath, Lavinia demands that the Primus of Ex Miscellanea approve each candidate, an approval that cannot be had, and voids it. Uproar follows; their peers leave, and Julius wins the certamen against the eldest open opponent.
stages.turned: Well argued, the doubts spread: senior magi withdraw, leaving a controversial venture, and elders pledge to take it to the Grand Tribunal.

stages.title: The Armada Sails
stages.clues: Two large ships, each under a modified Aegis of the Hearth giving +75 Magic Resistance, with strong wards against fire and a Muto Herbam spell giving +20 Soak. Icelandic seers grow uneasy at omens of death.
stages.ignored: The crusaders sail, not knowing what they face unless told.
stages.stopped: If the characters gave Vindolanda as a base, there is no armada: the first strike kills many leading magicians. If the Aegis at Scartaris is not raised to 75th level, Bard may flood it.
stages.turned: Warned, Bard and Pan Caudarax prepare and tell Vindsvall and the Gray Bull. The magi can teach Parma quickly, but their best advice to the galdramen is to hide. Grogs and companions sent alone escape the watchers.

stages.title: Assault on the Guardians
stages.clues: As the coast rises Pan Caudarax sends drake images to test the ships, then becomes a lindorm and dives.
stages.ignored: The Host breaks on the wards, too many to kill, while the dragon strikes from below as a kraken and is repelled. He may die, unless the Host heals him. Then Vindsvall's storm breaks one ward; the Host's winds sink that ship with about seven magi and most mundanes, and a spontaneous Kill the Living Air with two rooks of vis drains him. The last ship anchors in the southeast, where the Gray Bull, if free, may smash it.
stages.stopped: If the guardians repel them, they go home and by next summer try another way (see Hermetic Foothold). The Bull smashes through the ward, and a ship still afloat has two rounds to cut anchor and make open water. If both ships go, only Leap of Homecoming and the like save anyone.
stages.turned: Albinus drives off the Host and can bottle Vindsvall, and has an even chance against the Bull. If he captures it the crusaders land, and Bard waits as the giants arm.

stages.title: Hermetic Foothold
stages.clues: If repelled, Bonisagus magi guess that Bjornaer in animal form will escape the guardians' notice; they do.
stages.ignored: The materials for a Hermes Portal are ferried to the remote southeastern highlands. A strong force steps through, conjures a Mystic Tower, casts an Aegis of the Hearth and starts hunting. If the crusaders got past the guardians, they simply build it.
stages.stopped: Vindolanda may disrupt the ritual and keep the main force out.

stages.title: The Night of Tears
stages.clues: Under illusion, magi question mundanes by magic and find several galdramen, witches and seithkona.
stages.ignored: In one night they fall on twelve farmsteads and kill everyone. Warned at the last moment, Biorn Egilsson stands before his farm and asks Julius in Latin to talk; Julius burns him through his Ol-spirit, and the farm dies with him. The magi withdraw to their base. Talk of foreign Latin magi may now expose Vindolanda.

stages.title: The Grapes of Wrath
stages.clues: Ten galdramen, twelve seithkona and two trollsynir lie dead among over 120 farmers, labourers and kin, with three priests, one a son of Bishop Magnus Gizurarson. With no one owning the deed, Icelanders call it cowardly murder.
stages.ignored: The landvaettir lords vow revenge for Biorn; after giants and trollsynir die, the giant families rally to Bard; the Bishop of Skalholt calls all Christians to find the killers. Every galdraman gets an attendant spirit of Might equal to Song Talent x 5 for the war, cutting his casting to the spell phase, and it asks little or no vis.
stages.turned: Crusader characters may press for moderation.

stages.title: The Battle for Iceland
stages.clues: Vigdis warns that Julius has found Scartaris and strikes in three days. Bard plans to hit the tower while Julius is at Vindolanda, his vanguard flying there as eagles; Norns coordinate.
stages.ignored: Gull needs seven strikes on the Aegis and falls to six vis-backed Clenching Hand of the Crushed Heart spells. Bard takes up the hammer under a rain of spells while the Host shields him, unless Albinus banishes it.
stages.stopped: Crusader Victory: Bard falls and the Hermetics clear Iceland of magicians, while Lavinia finds that none knew of an Order of Odin. Policy may turn to offers of membership. The Icelanders now know who did it, and bringing such condemnation is itself a Hermetic crime; if the hreppur tried to join, the Grand Tribunal may call the crusade illegal.
stages.turned: Bard is Victorious: the seventh blow shatters the ward, over a hundred giants storm in and the Host rips the tower apart. A few magi flee by the Portal or Leap of Homecoming. Julius, if alive, is taken at sunset for the Yfel lords.

stages.title: The Battle Comes Home
stages.clues: Either way Bishop Magnus goes to Bremen, and with the archbishop to Rome, to ask the Pope to act.
stages.ignored: If Bard won, galdramen and giants raid Hermetic covenants, Pan Caudarax's mate joining as guardian if he is dead. Unchecked, the raids bring the full Order, which Iceland cannot withstand. If the Pope agrees, he excommunicates all Christian magi and forbids Christians to serve or trade with them, perhaps for years.
stages.stopped: If Bard won with Albinus's help, the Icelanders may be talked into Hermetic justice instead of raids.

stages.title: The Resolution
stages.clues: Pressure builds for a settlement.
stages.ignored: Hermetic Domination: with no real pressure, clearance goes on and Iceland empties for a land-rush. Mundane hatred lasts decades or centuries, and the landvaettir never forgive, though newcomers may strike their own treaties.
stages.stopped: Hermetic Failure with indiscriminate raids: the Order calls the crusade justified and strikes in full, and almost surely wins. House Jerbiton gets the excommunication lifted, and an inquiry into sorcery by Icelandic clergy closes both cathedral magic schools.
stages.turned: Hermetic Failure with no raids, or raids only on the guilty: sooner or later the Order seeks peace. The primi of Guernicus, Bonisagus and Jerbiton send emissaries, who land unchallenged and go before Bishop Magnus. Pressure on Julius and Lavinia can force the same talks.

stages.title: The Settlement
stages.clues: Bishop Magnus chairs the talks, on three options: the hreppur joins House Ex Miscellanea; it is recognised with a treaty of mutual protection; or it joins as a new House, keeping its own laws in Iceland.
stages.ignored: The Order wants the first if there were any raids, and fights the second; the hreppur wants the second; the third needs skilled bargaining. A past refusal of admission undercuts the emissaries.
stages.stopped: Icelanders demand compensation for every dead or hurt countryman; Bard demands it for the giants, and a separate treaty, which the new galdramen leader makes a condition. With raids, the Order wants its own losses paid. Each body's rank is argued for days.
stages.turned: Outlawry is argued: Hermetic killers of Icelanders if they return, Icelandic killers within a league of a covenant they attacked. The Order wants it limited to killers of mundanes and wider for Icelanders. The less wanton side has the edge. The bishop writes to the Pope for absolution.

links.note: The crusade's spirit master, or its enemy
Warns of the attack on Scartaris
Bishop Magnus's seat; the Gray Bull's pasture

neighbours.secrets:
Land of Fire & Ice pp. 29 and 63 foresee this war: killing great galdramen enrages the landvaettir lords, killing trollsynir enrages the giants, and the hreppur is the nearest thing to an Order of Odin that exists. The saga there is not official history (p. 67), and neither is this.

Land of Fire & Ice p. 70 tells of a separate voyage: in 1218 another ship of Flambeau magi from Bergen burns, and Einar Gamlisson's family dies with them. Hadrianus's is the voyage of 1214.

At the War Tribunal the characters may keep quiet, which the winner will remember; aid the crusade out of duty, ignorance or fear, for who else destroyed those covenants; or try for peace, which for Vindolanda means showing that it survives (p. 3). Many there want a hunt, glory or new vis, whatever is said. Whether Julius and Lavinia are renounced, punished or pardoned after a crusade ruled illegal is the storyguide's; their followers share it by rank (pp. 12-13).

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Ghost in the Isles
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. On a journey in the Scottish isles the characters find Hadrianus's ghost themselves, carry the warning to the Order, and stand high in the crusading party for it.

(Icelandic Wars p. 2)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Asking the Dragon
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda. Asked why he killed the archmagus, Pan Caudarax vaguely recalls his watchers warning of very strong, very hostile wizards, so he brought all his force. He owes nothing for slaying raiders, resents any notion that he serves an order of wizards, knows nothing of an Order of Odin and has small interest in Norse wizards.

(Icelandic Wars p. 2)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Vindolanda's Secret
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. No outsider suspects the covenant lies in Iceland. Do its magi stay hidden, or show their hand and argue that Hadrianus's death had nothing to do with an Order of Odin? Speaking means admitting that it still exists over three hundred years after its reported fall, but others will rally to it if it stands up.

(Icelandic Wars p. 3)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Scrying on the Doubters
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Some magi say the Order of Odin is a myth, so they must be fooled or in league with it. Loyal magi should look into their contacts, and the danger may excuse a little scrying.

(Icelandic Wars p. 3)

details.antagonist: Magi who call the Order of Odin a myth

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Hreppur Takes the Oath
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. Before the Tribunal the characters may propose that the whole hreppur joins the Order, which would make the war illegal under the Code. Proud Norsemen who refuse any jarl or king balk at serving a primus.

(Icelandic Wars p. 3-4)

details.antagonist: The pride of the hreppur, then Lavinia

stages.title: Win over the hreppur
stages.clues: The galdramen fear for their independence.
stages.ignored: The hreppur stays outside the Order.
stages.turned: It swears, and the news is brought to the War Tribunal, catching Julius and Lavinia off guard.

stages.title: Lavinia's ruling
stages.clues: She recovers fast, insisting that the Primus of Ex Miscellanea approve each candidate, an approval that cannot be had (see her record).
stages.ignored: The membership is void. Senior magi dispute it; their peers leave Julius and Lavinia, and a certamen settles it for Julius.

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Vindolanda as Base
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, with the crusade. With Vindolanda as a base the force skips the guardians and, on the characters' information, kills many leading magicians in its first strike. Bard's counter likely fails against Scartaris and Iceland falls quickly, unless no one thought to raise the Aegis to 75th level, in which case he may flood the place. Stage that while the characters are away, so they survive. Bishop Magnus's delegation sails either way.

(Icelandic Wars p. 4)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Lavinia's Demand
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. If the characters have shown their tie to Iceland, Lavinia orders their cooperation within a season. Defiance costs them the mainland site: Iain can have the gate spirit swallow the gatestone on one side and bring it out on the other, sealing Scartaris off. If they stayed hidden, the mainland site keeps them informed of the crusade.

(Icelandic Wars p. 4)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Scouting Iceland
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Scouts are wanted. Magi meet Pan Caudarax and may die as Hadrianus did, but if they seem weak he plays with them: he denies serving the Order of Odin, calls the killing his own choice and their lives forfeit, then lets them go home, or lets the persuasive land on an oath of good conduct. Grogs and companions alone slip past the watchers, and may find Vindolanda on the Snaefellsnes if it is a non-player covenant.

(Icelandic Wars p. 5)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Casting Tokens
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. Magi whose ties stayed secret may get people aboard. One who takes part in an Aegis casting, gets its tokens and brings them to Pan Caudarax puts the armada in grave danger.

(Icelandic Wars p. 7)

details.antagonist: The crusaders of the Order of Hermes

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Freeing the Gray Bull
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. The magi are asked to free the Bull, and Bishop Magnus will not lose his prize stud for less than an irresistible offer, so it means a raid.

(Icelandic Wars p. 7-8)

stages.title: The raid
stages.clues: A raid is not shameful in itself, but this target will hardly defend itself, so it may look cowardly; provoking a man as strong in law as a storgodi may also look bold.
stages.ignored: The Bull stays tame.
stages.turned: Outside the Dominion it bellows, the Host feeds it Might, and over a matter of weeks, faster in a magical aura, it regains its full size and strides into the highlands (Land of Fire & Ice p. 112).

stages.title: The case
stages.clues: It is the talk of Iceland for years.
stages.ignored: The raid's leader faces outlawry; supporters must be gathered at once.
stages.stopped: Even a settlement that avoids outlawry costs dear in compensation.

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Traitors in the Fleet
neighbours.summary:
For the crusade. Traitors have joined the expedition. Can the characters find them and their plan before the fleet is lost?

(Icelandic Wars p. 8)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Arming the Guardians
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. With casting tokens Pan Caudarax capsizes one ship easily; the other's counterattack may kill or drive him off, and Vindsvall or the Bull finishes it. Level 85 Creo Vim or Rego Vim potions would also take him through the wards.

(Icelandic Wars p. 9)

details.antagonist: The crusaders of the Order of Hermes

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Saving the Drowning
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Quick thought and spontaneous magic may save magi and grogs from certain death and hold down the losses.

(Icelandic Wars p. 9)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Masters of Spirits
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. This stage turns on spirit magic, above all Albinus's. Characters very strong in Vim, with the right spells, may shift the balance as he does.

(Icelandic Wars p. 9)

details.antagonist: The guardians, the galdramen and the giants of Iceland
