neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Disrupting the Portal
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. The magi learn of the Hermes Portal and may be a match for the Bjornaer casting it. Acting fast, they might break the ritual and bar the main force.

(Icelandic Wars p. 9)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Envoys to Sinus Wodinis
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. The characters are sent to ask the Bjornaer of Sinus Wodinis for help against the Order of Odin. They dislike strangers and may be allied with Norse wizards; one may even be a trollson.

(Icelandic Wars p. 9)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Testing the Bonisagus Theory
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Bjornaer characters test whether heart-beasts pass the guardians, then help defend the Hermes Portal ritual and guard the base while it is raised.

(Icelandic Wars p. 9)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Gunnar's Daughter
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. A late rider, a chance to mend the magi's name with a church warden, and a raid they did not expect. Iceland being Iceland, such a gift is nearly sure to be repaid.

(Icelandic Wars p. 10)

details.antagonist: The crusaders of the Order of Hermes

stages.title: Gunnar rides to Dagverdara
stages.clues: Gunnar Loftursson asks for a magus at once: Asta's skill cannot save their dying daughter, and she needs ond (vis) for Biarg spirits, in Hermetic terms Creo, Corpus or Vim.
stages.ignored: The child and her mother are left to the crusaders.
stages.turned: The magi give vis or ride back with him.

stages.title: The church
stages.clues: Warned by her fylgja an hour ahead, Asta and the women take to the church, where she sings on, exhausted, to keep the Biarg spirit with the girl.
stages.ignored: As Gunnar returns, a Hermetic party faces the household's men before the door.

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Witch's Heart
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Lavinia sends the characters to a western-quarter farmstead to kill a witch, bring her heart so she may question the ghost, and leave no witnesses. The galdrakona's fylgja warns her; she and the women bar themselves in the church with the children as the men take up arms. Neither is a danger to magi. Will they murder in cold blood? Mentem magic leaves the question of who kills her, and whether inside the church or out.

(Icelandic Wars p. 10)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Moderating the Crusade
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. A plan that kills dozens of mundanes looks close to interfering with the mundanes, ethics aside. Uneasy magi may persuade the crusaders to hold back.

(Icelandic Wars p. 10)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Hidden Covenant
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Julius orders the characters to find a Hermetic covenant said to lie in the western quarter. Spirits and mundanes are watching for foreigners. A magus caught outside an Aegis at sunrise or sunset may be attacked with his Parma down, and grogs and companions without resistance at any time.

(Icelandic Wars p. 10-11)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Combined Assault
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. Bard, Gull and Vigdis come to the magi: Julius will attack Scartaris in three days, and the tower is to be struck while he does. The magi must hold him there; Vigdis can give each a landvaettir of Might 50, and Orlog-spirits may let them lay an ambush or a trap.

Julius and his retinue have strong Parma, though vis-boosted spells pass it, and the hoplites' wards cover mundane weapons. Above the sanctum sit thousands of tons of ice: tunnelling and Creo Ignem may flood Scartaris in an instant with plain water, and the blow alone should kill. If they are losing, landvaettir throw themselves before spells and earth spirits may carry them away through the mountain; they may yet be captured or killed.

(Icelandic Wars p. 11-12)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Smuggling the Galdramen
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. Survivors may use the gateway to get galdramen off the island, while trollsynir and giants shapeshift and flee, many to Helluland. Only mainland Hermetic support can stop the killing, perhaps by raising mundane anger, and Bishop Magnus's delegation is the best tool for that.

(Icelandic Wars p. 13)

details.antagonist: The crusaders of the Order of Hermes

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Hornet's Nest
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. The magic is won, but with no proof of a threat the campaign looks empty, and mundane anger may bring Hermetic charges. If the hreppur tried to join, every crusader may be in deep trouble. Time to negotiate a peace?

(Icelandic Wars p. 13)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Into the Tower
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. Not being magical creatures, the magi can carry the fight inside the Aegis, with penalties, or supply potions and other magics for Bard's forces.

(Icelandic Wars p. 13)

details.antagonist: The crusaders of the Order of Hermes

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Flight from Iceland
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Away scouting when the base falls, the characters must get off the island before they share their comrades' fate.

(Icelandic Wars p. 13)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Hostages of Iceland
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Galdramen and landvaettir capture the characters, and Yfel spirits suppress their Gifts for a time. There are no prisons: on an oath of good conduct they live in a household and work for their food. Treated well, those who keep faith may teach Latin and letters and end up more guests than hostages. Escape is impossible without help, and attacking the householder is unwise.

Not for every troupe, and not for those guilty of cowardly butchery, who die once they are named.

(Icelandic Wars p. 13)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Raiding Party
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda, against the crusade. Asked to join a raid, with rich loot, will the magi take part in murderous vengeance? Refusal may offend and look suspicious, and random attacks would bring ruin. Most neutral magi would accept a strike on the guilty as justice, and Orlog spirits can arrange ambushes; a precise vendetta costs little support but makes Hermetic justice less likely.

Instead they may urge the Icelanders to seek that justice: the landvaettir could be called faeries, and the crusaders plainly interfered with mundanes, so renunciation has a case. Icelanders will dislike it unless Hermetic help won their victory.

(Icelandic Wars p. 14)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Ambush on the Road
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Expedition members are ambushed and killed as they travel. The characters must take care, not knowing what form the attack will take.

(Icelandic Wars p. 14)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Bishop's Delegation
neighbours.summary:
For anyone. The characters hear of Bishop Magnus's journey. They may want it stopped, but how, without making things worse?

(Icelandic Wars p. 14)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Vindolanda at the Table
neighbours.summary:
For Vindolanda. Magi who sided fully with the hreppur have great influence. If they taught galdramen Parma or Hermetic magic, the emissaries insist that the galdramen join the Order. If renounced they are reinstated on request. If they backed the crusade they may return to Scartaris, but lose any vis source the hreppur gave.

(Icelandic Wars p. 15)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: The Envoy's Mission
neighbours.summary:
For crusaders. Proven characters may join the envoys. Former prisoners, who know Icelandic ways, may be released and offered a place at the table.

(Icelandic Wars p. 15)

neighbours.name: Icelandic Wars: Galdor into Theory
neighbours.summary:
For anyone. If the hreppur joins, Albinus works to bring galdor magic into Hermetic Theory. If he succeeds, galdramen may learn Hermetic Theurgy and Hermetic theurgists may summon landvaettir.

(Icelandic Wars p. 15)

neighbours.name: The harbour of De Panne
neighbours.summary: The harbour of the town of De Panne.

neighbours.name: The harbour of Exeter
neighbours.summary: The harbour of the town of Exeter.

neighbours.name: The harbour of Bergen
neighbours.summary: The harbour of the town of Bergen.

characters.name: Markus of Verditius
characters.summary: The leader of Wormhout: a thickset man of average height, dark brown hair and green eyes, an expert in sacred architecture.
characters.secrets:
Looks 35. Size 0, Confidence 3, Twilight Points 9. Reputations: Contemptibly Cautious 3 with Flambeau and Tytalus magi; Promising Theoretician 2 with Verditius and Bonisagus magi (p. 78).

A Vim specialist who has so far escaped temporary Twilight by caution and luck, though the last brush nearly took him. He knows few spells and invests a device with any effect he wants. He commissioned his longevity potion from the Order's foremost Verditius alchemist. He dreads casting the Aegis, which his enduring magic lets last up to ten years, and is researching a way to master rituals and cast them safely.

characters.name: Vera of Bonisagus
characters.summary: A thin, tiny woman with greying blond hair and blue eyes, and an important powerbroker in the Normandy Tribunal.
characters.secrets:
Looks 50. Size -1, Confidence 3, Twilight Points 15. Reputation: Formidable 3 with the Normandy Tribunal (p. 78).

Her high ideals have made her enemies, even among quaesitores. Her law, certamen and, rarely for a Bonisagus, Wizard's War impress even Flambeau and Tytalus. She specialises in deception and illusion, which her master taught as the proof that truth is hard won, and uses them to expose lies. She often goes with Iphimedeia on investigations.

characters.name: Iphimedeia of Guernicus
characters.summary: A quaesitor: a tall, strongly built woman with light brown hair and brown eyes, often called on to look into Hermetic crimes.
characters.secrets:
Looks 40. Size 0, Confidence 3, Twilight Points 17. Reputations: Impartial 3 with the Normandy Tribunal; Dangerous 3 with guilty magi (p. 78). The book calls her a quaesitor on p. 75.

Respected, with powerful enemies made by her impartial justice. An Intellego specialist, sharpened by her rivalry with Vera. Few in Normandy doubt she can find a sigil on illegal magic however old, and several Marched magi have found illusion and masking useless before her (pp. 78-79).

characters.name: Cornelius of Verditius
characters.summary: The youngest magus of Wormhout: a lean, shortish man with black hair and green eyes, a maker of automata.
characters.secrets:
Looks 32. Size 0, Confidence 3, Twilight Points 10. Reputations: Apolitical 2 and Maker of Automata 3, both with the Normandy Tribunal (p. 79).

He wants an automaton that truly learns, which no Hermetic maga has made; his best play chess and work puzzles. They watch the covenant's vis sources, with magic from Vera and Iphimedeia that stays hidden and pierces concealment, on covenant land only and against concealments only. Some call that scrying; Iphimedeia would argue that entering under concealment is itself magical spying. No test case has been brought.

characters.name: Iain the Scot

description.biography:
Magical equipment (p. 133): a dirk enchanted for +4 damage and never to break; half chain made light (load -0.5) with +2 protection; a Ring of Magic Resistance giving +50, commissioned from a Verditius in 869 AD, which works only for members of Vindolanda; several Rings of Ages that make him look other ages, at present about 50. He keeps healing potions by him: one stabilized his wounds and the fire destroyed the rest.

The block's Cursed (lost his gift) -6 has no catalog entry and is kept here; Wealthy Merchant +3 is Wealthy and Merchant.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 442 as printed (looks 29); Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 5. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Enemies: servants of Hetep.
Abilities: Boating 4 to Profession: Boatman; Legend Lore 6 to Area Lore: Iceland; Scribe Greek 5 to Artes Liberales; Scribe Latin 6 to Artes Liberales.

Abilities renamed: European Area Lore 4 to Area Lore: Europe; Mediterranean Area Lore 4 to Area Lore: Mediterranean.

Abilities with no counterpart: Alchemy's 75 xp spent on Philosophiae.

reputations.name: Fair Dealer (London, Flanders, Venice and Constantinople merchants)

characters.summary: A big, well-kept merchant of De Panne in Flanders, known as a fair dealer from London to Constantinople, with light red hair and blue eyes and no scar worth the name. He says little of himself and cares most for his family.
characters.secrets:
Iain the Unbowed, filius and son of Liam the Shapeless, an original member of Vindolanda, and now a natural magician. Born in 778, he looks 29 without his rings. Hetep maimed his Gift in Pralix's war and Setna alone can restore it (pp. 72, 77, 88, 129). After more than a hundred years' study he has the basics of Natural Magic. He serves Victor and his family with equal devotion, and hides his age and his past from the world (p. 133).

He guarded the Scartaris gatestone from 888, settled in De Panne in 1182, and after 1220 runs Vindolanda's daily affairs for Victor (pp. 72, 77, 87).

characters.name: Victor filius Pralix

description.biography:
The book prints no Arts, Abilities, Virtues or Flaws: his powers, with his Magic Might of 50, are his block (p. 135).
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 438 as printed (looks 41); Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 6. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.

characters.summary: A follower of Pralix, given his sigil when she defeated Damhan-Allaidh in 816, whom the Order has long counted among the dead.
characters.secrets:
In life he could bring anyone round to any position, with an understanding of people unmatched in his day, but a demon was beyond him. Hetep overwhelmed him and shut him in a hellish dream, where he suffered for sixty years until he outwitted the demon and seized the dreamscape. Since then each has argued the other's soul in the language of dreams, over grace and its rejection; Victor now rules the dream and Hetep must endure his constant calls to renounce Hell (p. 135).

Spirit and body are parted, though he is technically alive, and the body would crumble within weeks if his ward failed, so he works by possession alone. Brighde, his friend's granddaughter, comes first, but everything he does bends toward destroying the Spider, and he will draw the magi into risky schemes in return for scraps of knowledge about Damhan-Allaidh or Hetep (pp. 135-136).

He looks a tall man in Roman robes, frozen in the ward in his Scartaris laboratory (p. 82). Founder and Disceptator of Vindolanda, he entered the battle of wills in 888 (p. 72). Born in 782.

The book calls him founder of House Ex Miscellanea (pp. 84, 88). That is a title for a leading figure of the House: Pralix founded the Ordo Miscellanea and was its prima (p. 71; Heirs to Merlin p. 13).

Magic Might 50. Possession (ReMe 50, cost varies): any human in eye contact, or in sight of his body. Entry costs Might equal to the victim's Confidence + Stamina (+3 if Strong-Willed) + twice any True Faith. Parma Magica resists, using the highest of Corpus, Mentem or Vim, against his penetration of 50 + stress die; a Natural Resistance roll (Stamina + stress die) of 50 also stops it. In a Gifted host he uses his full magic without Might. He does not want a stolen body, and takes control or searches a mind only at need.

Morphean Landscape (ReMe, 10 points): melds the dreams of up to twelve people into one under his control, for meetings. Mastery of the Mind (Me): any Mentem spell to level 50, including his own, and the Oneiromantic spells of The Mysteries if the troupe uses them. Mastery of the Image (Im): the same with Imaginem to level 30. Mastery of the Forms: other Forms to level 15. Each costs twice the spell's magnitude in Might, with no words or gestures, only a moment's thought.

characters.name: Lord Peter

description.biography:
Printed combat: Brawl (fist) Init +4 Atk +4 Dfn +3 Dam +1; Dagger +6, +5, +6, +3; Longsword +9, +8, +10, +4. Soak +15 with his magical cloak. Printed as Landed Knight, Virtues Demonic Familiar +4 and Blackmail +2: the catalog has them as Landed Noble and as Minor Flaws. Reckless +1, printed among his Virtues and Flaws, is a Personality Trait. English Law is Common Law, and his Guile's specialty is as printed. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious; Body OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Incapacitated. LFI p. 83.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 39 as printed; Twilight Points 0 / 3 = Warping 0; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 4. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Blackmail: Falkes de Bréauté, acting Earl of Devonshire; Susceptible to Divine Power as Susceptibility to Divine Power; Bad Reputation dropped (kept as the Reputation it printed); Dark Secret: diabolist; Obligations as Dutybound: to Hell.
Abilities: Occult Lore 6 to Infernal Lore; Scribe Latin 2 to Artes Liberales; Weapon and Shield 5 to Single Weapon.

characters.summary: A landed knight of Devon, tall and thin, with Norman features and a short black beard, who usually wears a long red cloak. His family came to England with the Conqueror.
characters.secrets: An English diabolist, promised more magical power for freeing Hetep. Found his grandfather's occult books on his death; Hell has watched his family since an ancestor served Damhan-Allaidh near Carnac. He blackmails Falkes de Bréauté, acting Earl of Devonshire (p. 83). The characters kill him in the opening adventure (p. 76).

characters.name: Brighde Scot

description.biography:
Fully grown she will have Str -1, Dex -1, Qik 0 and Size 0. Soak -2. Printed Virtue Charm +1 has no catalog counterpart and is left out. Her Gift comes from p. 87; the block prints only Latent Magical Ability. Fatigue OK, -3, -5, Unconscious; Body OK, -3, -5, Incapacitated. LFI p. 84.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 5 as printed; Twilight Points 0 / 3 = Warping 0; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 4. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Incredible Intelligence as Great Intelligence.
Abilities: Scribe Latin 1 to Artes Liberales; Disputatio 1 to Teaching.

characters.summary: A very bright child of De Panne, daughter of Donncadh Scot and granddaughter of the merchant Iain, who already has some Latin and is learning her letters.
characters.secrets:
Her magical potential is plain to any magus in five minutes. Her grandfather has shown her the Scartaris sanctum, and she dreams of being a wizard like him (p. 84). She has the Gift (p. 87).

Kidnapped by Lord Peter and forced to open the gate; possessed by Hetep; then host to Victor, who imprisons the demon in her and takes her as his apprentice. He hates controlling her and does so only at need. Her gauntlet is the story of 1240. A player may run her, but she does not adventure before that gauntlet (p. 87).

characters.name: Pralix
characters.summary: The Tytalus maga who first beat Damhan-Allaidh and founded House Ex Miscellanea.
characters.secrets: Victor's parens. Landed in Northumbria in May 814, beat Damhan-Allaidh in 816, and raised the Ordo Miscellanea from the witches, druids, beast mages and spirit masters of her army, becoming prima when it joined the Order (p. 71). Heirs to Merlin p. 13 has the Ordo founded in 815 and accepted in 817, a year inside this book's campaign of 814 to 816; this pack follows 815.

characters.name: Ealasaid, Lady of the Waters
characters.summary: A theurgist of the old covenant of Vindolanda, long dead.
characters.secrets: Her line came down from the Romano-Celtic priests of Sulis Minerva at Bath. She worked out the Carnac gate and rebuilt the gatestones as Hermetic thaumaturgy. Filia of Morwena and parens of Macomb. She fled Wales from threats by Diedne magi, reclaimed her lands with a first sanctum under Glyder Fawr, left it to Macomb, and moved to the Sea Temple beneath the sea off Devon. Damhan-Allaidh killed her there in 889, and her ghost brought the dome down on him and Liam (pp. 71-73, 88, 94, 123).

characters.name: Macomb
characters.summary: A theurgist of the old covenant of Vindolanda, long dead.
characters.secrets: Ealasaid's filius and an original member, whose sanctum was Glyder Fawr in Snowdonia. Damhan-Allaidh killed him there in 889 (pp. 71-72, 94-95).

characters.name: Blund Thorgilsson

description.biography:
Land of Fire & Ice p. 99. The book prints no Abilities.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 32 as printed; Twilight Points 0 / 3 = Warping 0; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 3. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.

characters.summary: A storbondi of northern Snaefellsnes, tall, dark-haired and brown-eyed, rich and influential, with several tenancies and the local church.
characters.secrets: He hates magicians and needs one: his priest has failed him and he is growing desperate. He killed a local witch in mistaken revenge, so the hreppur left him to suffer (pp. 98, 105). Years later Einar turns him against the eggs (p. 114). If he hurts one of Pan Caudarax's brood he has few days left (p. 115).

characters.name: Una

description.biography:
Land of Fire & Ice p. 99. The book prints no Abilities.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 22 as printed; Twilight Points 0 / 3 = Warping 0; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 1. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.

characters.summary: Blund Thorgilsson's young wife, of average height with light brown hair and green eyes, mother of two daughters aged four and two.
characters.secrets: She has miscarried twice in a year and is pregnant again without knowing it (p. 99). Her cat Hlokk guards her.

characters.name: Signy Grettisdottir
characters.summary: A member of the galdramen hreppur's council.
characters.secrets: A trollsdottir of the council: printed Magic Resistance 63, dropped as no hedge wizard has one (Hedge Magic RE p. 9), Size +2, looks 37, printed Confidence 3. Her giant mother raised her and she never met her outlawed father. She picked fights until age taught her some caution, and trollsynir magic has left her looking more troll than human. She has come to back her descendant Arnor Arngeirsson in his dispute, and the attack on the eggs worries her (p. 103).

characters.name: Arnor Arngeirsson
characters.summary: A member of the galdramen hreppur's council.
characters.secrets: Leader of the few vitkir left: Size +1, looks 67, printed Confidence 4. His temple lies in a regio near his farm, and such regiones are rare and precious to vitkir, who must keep their rites wholly secret. Wanting back those that have left vitkir hands, for vitkir lately fled from Norway, he blights fields and cattle to force sales and hides it from his victims' fylgjur. A galdraman has reported him. He will answer that the victims never suspected and that he paid fair prices (p. 103).

characters.name: Leif Beogart
characters.summary: Attends the hreppur at Eldborg.
characters.secrets: A vitki of the powerful Beogart family, in a feud of centuries with the Odd-Karnors. Size +0, printed Confidence 4. He has come only to make plain that he had no part in the attack on the eggs (p. 103).

characters.name: Biorn Egilsson
characters.summary: Leader of the galdramen hreppur.
characters.secrets: Iceland's oldest galdraman, a deft politician: Size +1, looks 85, printed Confidence 3, Twilight Points 19, which are Warping 6 now (DE p. 538). Most galdramen have made the long hamfaring (Final Twilight) by his age, and he knows his fylgja's call cannot be refused for ever. He wants peace for those to come, and finds the quarrel between the two Christian schools the hardest to settle (p. 104). He sees no reason the magi should not belong, and offers vis rights if they appease the dragon (p. 105).

characters.name: Father Halldor Ormsson
characters.summary: Represents the Holar school on the hreppur's council.
characters.secrets: Size +0, printed Confidence 3. He seems to want the balance kept, but his first aim is his school's right to harvest magical sites. Bishop Gudmund's troubles leave Holar to itself. When some Skalholt vis sites went unharvested, Holar claimed abandonment and took them. Some at Holar deny the hreppur's authority; Halldor thinks the moment is wrong, not the idea. The school seeks a breakthrough to the strength of the trollsynir and traditional galdramen, and with it would press for independence (p. 104).

characters.name: Father Vebrand Thoroddson
characters.summary: Represents the Skalholt school on the hreppur's council.
characters.secrets: Size +0, printed Confidence 2. Local priests gather the school's vis, and several have died of late, so sites stood idle until new priests came. Holar calls them abandoned. Vebrand hopes the hreppur rules against Holar, and it probably will, since abandonment normally means many years of disuse (p. 104).

characters.name: Aldis Kolbeinsdottir
characters.summary: Nominal leader of the Seithkona.
characters.secrets: Size -1, looks 75, printed Confidence 3. Her gloomy prophecies come true often enough that people listen, and some claim to have escaped disaster by solving her riddles, but she argues practical matters badly (p. 104).

characters.name: Helga Grimsdottir
characters.summary: Speaks for the Seithkona at the hreppur.
characters.secrets: Size +0, looks 51, printed Confidence 4. Being women, most Seithkona cannot attend, so they are always outvoted. For years she has proposed that the absent may hand their votes to those who go, which the powers at the hreppur will never pass, unless she brings every Seithkona in Iceland to one meeting (pp. 104-105).

characters.name: Solrun
characters.summary: A strikingly lovely woman with long golden hair, pale skin and very blue eyes, charming, guileless and full of stories.
characters.secrets: Bard's daughter, sent to bring the characters to his feast; she calls herself his servant. She treats every admirer alike. She is a giantess with the Jotunn Affinity with Frost and the Healer talent, and turns up at need to rescue guests from the trolls (pp. 107-108, 112).

characters.name: Thordis
characters.summary: A golden-haired daughter of Bard Snaefellsass.
characters.secrets: Paired with the party's leader at the feast, where she proposes the toast to the guests (p. 109). See Bard's Daughters.

characters.name: Helga Bardsdottir
characters.summary: The eldest of Bard Snaefellsass's nine daughters, who does not live with him.
characters.secrets: She has substantial magic, and quarrels constantly with a father much like her. Red-Cloak, Thorkel's eldest son, is drawn to her and cannot admit it, so it comes out as rivalry and spite: he once set her adrift on an ice floe in a storm (pp. 112-113).

characters.name: Jarl Agdi
characters.summary: Geirrod's lieutenant, a troll.
characters.secrets: He rules Geirrod's people with an iron fist (p. 118).

characters.name: Kar Liefsson
characters.summary: A peddler of household goods who carries the Snaefellsnes gossip from farm to farm.
characters.secrets: He brings word of the dragon rumour and of Blund's tall machine, and nearly took a beating for asking about it (p. 114).

characters.name: Thorodd Gamlisson
characters.summary: A farmer on the north side of Snaefell who keeps his own counsel.
characters.secrets: Einar's brother. He says nothing of Einar until threatened, by force or magic. Then he says Einar has gone back to the Glittering Plains, beyond reach, and under more pressure that the way in lies in Snaefell's central crater. He knows nothing but the reasons for the vendetta (p. 115).

characters.name: Eleanor, Iain's wife

description.biography:
Her looks owe seven years to a longevity potion from her husband (p. 134). No Confidence is printed.

The block's Empathy +1 is the Fourth Edition Talent, not the catalog's Empathy (a Major Faerie Method), and is kept here. Bad Reputation -1 has no catalog entry and prints no Reputation to keep: some women of the town hold her birth against her.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 47 as printed (looks 40); Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Oversensitive (Minor): snide comments.

Abilities renamed: Craft Toys 5 to Craft: Toys.

characters.summary: Wife of the merchant Iain Scot of De Panne: still a striking beauty close on fifty, dressed in the newest fashion. A foundling left at St Michael's church and fostered by a carpenter through Father Galcher, she sold the toys she made at market for high prices until Iain, the town's best match, married her. Some women of the town still look down on her for her birth.

characters.name: Donncadh Scot

description.biography:
Magical equipment (p. 134): half chain made light (load -0.5) with +2 protection; a Ring of Magic Resistance of +20, made by Iain.

characters.summary: Iain's son and partner at De Panne, a very tall man of 28 with light brown hair and blue eyes, known among Flemish merchants as a fair trader, with a young daughter, Brighde.
characters.secrets: A natural magician with the Gift (p. 87), and consors of Vindolanda (p. 80), frantic to rescue Brighde in 1220. He knows his father's secret and has been taught by him in the Scartaris library. He tells nothing of the gateway or of Scartaris unless he must, and then the least he can. Hermetic magi make him a little nervous and their magic fascinates him. He would once have made a fine apprentice and might even now learn the Arts, but he would not take an apprentice's place (p. 134).

She is delighted with her marriage, expecting a second child, a proud mother and known among the merchants' wives for her close interest in everyone's affairs, though not in the family trade.
characters.secrets: She knows nothing of Iain's true past or her husband's magic; recent events, and arriving at a Hermetic covenant, have shaken her badly. Her fylgja (p. 32) is a hawk. She has never linked her little accidents to coming danger, so it spent the past week trying and failing to warn her (pp. 134-135).

characters.name: Einar Gamlisson

description.biography:

Enchanting Music, Summoning and Hamfarir came by initiation, though the book's list of initiations has no Summoning (p. 50). The worked example on p. 48 gives him Com 2, Sing 8, Galdor Wisdom 8 and Ol-galdor 6 against this block's 5, 11, 12 and 5: this block is for 1231.

He should have many minor items, above all healing potions in the form of woven bandages (p. 139).

characters.summary: A distinguished Icelander who looks in his late fifties, with straight black hair, rare among the Norse, a neat beard, a blue robe embroidered in knots and a voice like honey that talks people round.
characters.secrets: A traditional galdraman and the main antagonist of the Fire and Song story arc, sworn against the dragon Pan Caudarax. In 1210 he went to Norway to help his kinsman Bjarke Odd-Karnor in a feud, and there married Yrsa and had two sons. In 1218 she sailed to join him on a ship that also carried Flambeau magi bound to destroy the Order of Odin. The landvaettir felt them, and the dragon burned the ship. Not seeing the dragon's reasons, Einar swore to destroy its family as his was destroyed (pp. 69-70). He is a great friend of the alfar and of the Norns; the Norn who became his fylgja showed him his own doom, so he hurries his revenge, and she now looks much like his dead wife (p. 140). His nidstong cursed Pan Caudarax's eggs (pp. 98, 100). He fled to Glasvellir, where he took a new wife and children in the human village, and in 1230 stirred Blund Thorgilsson against the eggs; Thorodd Gamlisson of Snaefell is his brother (pp. 114-117). If he lives he teaches the Aesir faith to Geirrod's slaves (p. 127).

characters.summary: A storgodi and the eldest legitimate son of Hvamm-Sturla and Gudny Bodvarsdottir of the Myramen. Marriage to Helga Arisdottir won him the estate of Stad at Snaefellsnes and half the Thorsnes godord; the priest Thorgils Snorrason gave him the other half. In 1220 he is the strongest man in southern Iceland, his brother Sighvat holds a like place in the north, and his youngest brother is Snorri Sturluson. He is known as fair by his thingmen, and as ambitious by everyone.
characters.secrets: He rides against Hetep's dead on Snaefellsnes with thirty men, takes ship with the magi, and gives out a tale the public can accept (pp. 86-87). He wants the foreign magi under his influence: he offers them law and his support as thingmen, sells Dagverdara, and lends them Vifil, who watches them for him (pp. 98-99).

characters.summary: A tall, thin, affable farmer and smith of Snaefellsnes with light brown hair, brown eyes and a clubfoot that keeps him from much farm work. His smithy makes tools and now and then weapons, and earns him well. His son runs the farm and its three laborers, and he is known for his generosity to neighbors in hard times.
characters.secrets: A moderately powerful traditional galdraman who quietly sells his services around the region. With the farm in his son's hands he means to work on his magic (p. 142). Thord asks him to guide the foreign magi, and to watch and report on them, which he admits only if asked; he has no Gentle Gift, so they may guess (p. 99). He can tell them about Pan Caudarax (p. 101), brings them to the hreppur, and shares the vis if he found the nidstong himself (pp. 102, 106).

characters.name: Hadrianus of Flambeau
characters.summary: An archmagus of House Flambeau, teacher of two filii.
characters.secrets:
In 1214 he heard of magicians working from Iceland and sailed from Bergen with his two filii. Their hostility roused the landvaettir watchers, and Pan Caudarax burned the ship. The filii died at once. Hadrianus lived through the flame and killed a band of landvaettir, then botched a spell and fell into brief Twilight, and was thrown in the sea and drowned (Icelandic Wars pp. 1-2).

His ghost haunts a Scottish island until 1224, when it tells a magus of Loch Leglean, incoherently, that forces of the Order of Odin killed him, and rests. A summoning to learn more sends him into Final Twilight (p. 2). He spoke of a dragon and other beasts, not of spirits, as the landvaettir took solid form to reach him past his Parma (p. 6).

Land of Fire & Ice p. 70 tells of a separate voyage, with no names: in 1218 other powerful Flambeau magi on a ship from Bergen drew the dragon's fire, and Einar Gamlisson's wife and sons died with them.

characters.name: Julius of Flambeau
characters.summary: An archmagus of House Flambeau, an Ignem specialist, whose strongest spells are made for hunting renounced magi.
characters.secrets:
After 1224 he rises to prominence and, with Lavinia, prepares the invasion of Iceland (Icelandic Wars p. 2). He is only average in Vim, and his Perdo Vim spells are against demons, not magical spirits (p. 6).

He beats the senior opponent of the crusade in certamen at the War Tribunal (p. 4), burns Biorn Egilsson as he asks to talk (p. 9), and leads the hoplites against Vindolanda (p. 12). If Bard wins and Julius lives, he is taken at sunset and given to the Yfel lords (p. 13).

characters.name: Lavinia of Guernicus
characters.summary: An archmaga and Quaesitor of House Guernicus, an Intellego specialist skilled in wards and necromancy.
characters.secrets:
With Julius she prepares the invasion. In 1230 she calls the War Tribunal at Durenmar, the domus magna of House Bonisagus in the Rhine Tribunal, open to all with an interest, to debate and organise a crusade against Iceland, and declares it legal and binding (Icelandic Wars pp. 2, 4). She has no offensive spells against magical spirits (p. 6).

If the hreppur swears the Oath she answers that joining a House needs its primus's consent, demands that the Primus of Ex Miscellanea approve each candidate, an approval that cannot be had, and declares the membership invalid (p. 4). She has witches' hearts brought to her to question their ghosts (p. 10). Her own divinations slowly show that Iceland's magicians knew nothing of any Order of Odin (p. 12).

The book prints that Primus as an unnamed, reclusive prima who refuses all contact as she readies for the doom she has foretold for decades, which is what makes the demand impossible (p. 4). In the Stonehenge Tribunal's Order, which this pack follows, Immanola entered Final Twilight in 1216 and Ebroin has held the office since, so a troupe must settle why his approval cannot be had.

characters.name: Albinus of Ex Miscellanea
characters.summary: An archmagus of House Ex Miscellanea, a Theban spirit master.
characters.secrets:
His spells can beat the guardians. If support for the crusade holds he sails with it, drives off the Host and can bottle Vindsvall; he has an even chance of stopping the Gray Bull (Icelandic Wars pp. 7-8).

If support is undermined he withdraws. If Lavinia rebuffs the hreppur he goes to Iceland, affirms its membership to the guardians and Biorn Egilsson, and with a laboratory from Vindolanda can make them magics against the crusade (p. 7). If the hreppur joins the Order he works to bring galdor into Hermetic Theory (p. 15).

characters.name: Gunnar Loftursson
characters.summary: A bondi of Snaefellsnes, warden of the local church, married to the galdrakona Asta.
characters.secrets: A neighbour of Dagverdara. His young daughter falls gravely ill during the war, and he rides to the magi for ond (Icelandic Wars p. 10).

characters.name: Asta
characters.summary: A young galdrakona, wife of Gunnar Loftursson, with a fylgja.
characters.secrets: Crusaders mark her for death. Warned by her fylgja, she keeps singing the spell that holds a Biarg spirit at her daughter's side from inside the church (Icelandic Wars p. 10).

characters.name: Vigdis
characters.summary: A Norn lady, a landvaettir lady of the Orlog spirits.
characters.secrets: With Bard and Gull she warns Vindolanda that Julius has found Scartaris and will strike in three days, and she can give each magus a landvaettir attendant of Might 50 (Icelandic Wars pp. 11-12).

books.name: Eyes of the Gnome
books.author: Timon, follower of Tremere
books.description: A spell of the Grimoire of the Hidden. InTe, R: Per, D: Sun, T: Spec. Sees through up to a thousand paces of rock and reads its formation, senses the stability of any part within 100 paces, and shows detail within 15 (p. 91).

books.author: Timon, follower of Tremere
books.description: A spell of the Grimoire of the Hidden. PeTe req Re, R: Touch, D: Spec, T: Spec. Destroys earth or rock before the caster as he walks, shoring the tunnel while the spell lasts, until he comes out or Sun duration ends. An unsupported tunnel may fall soon afterward; Eyes of the Gnome may find a route through stable rock (p. 91).

books.name: Soothing the Earth's Wound
books.author: Timon, follower of Tremere
books.description: A spell of the Grimoire of the Hidden. MuTe req Re, printed T: Touch, D: Sun/Inst, T: Spec. Turns the surfaces of a tunnel or chamber to clay and fuses the cracks, leaving an unbroken solid up to a pace thick. Best on rock; in earth it packs tight enough for dry ground, and vis makes the material granite, which holds even in earth (pp. 91-92).

books.name: Carve the Mystic Caverns
books.author: Timon, follower of Tremere
books.description: A spell of the Grimoire of the Hidden. PeTe req Mu, R: Touch, D: Inst, T: Str, Ritual. Carves a huge underground structure to the caster's complete design, changes the surrounding stone to granite, and may face it in any stone up to the finest marble and complex mosaic. Unlike Conjure the Mystic Tower it depends on the caster's skill: elaborate work may need Int + Architecture for lasting stability (p. 92).

He has not yet had to keep the oath (p. 140), and will raze the town only if the hoard is robbed (p. 63).

creatures.secrets: Born in 960 in Helluland, the giants' realm beyond Greenland, son of King Dumb, half giant and half troll, and of Mjoll, daughter of the frost giant Snaer the Old; fostered by giants in Iceland, he settled in Norway. A trollson in Ars Magica's terms, more human than giant after so long among men. He left Norway with so many others when Harald Finehair took the crown, came to Iceland with his nine daughters, named Snaefellsnes and made his home at Songhellir, the Singing Cave. His brother Thorkel settled with him; their families feuded and made peace. Having guarded the people there against the trolls that swarm in those parts, he is held their guardian spirit. He leads all Iceland's giants and is one of the land's Guardians (p. 141). He wants peace between the dragon and Einar, and counts himself guardian of the land where the characters' covenant stands (p. 70). creatures.secrets:
Earth daemons of Thoth, each with its own name, akin to the Amphisbaena of Hedge Magic p. 76 but far greater. They dug secret tunnels and hid things in remote caves for him, and helped his priests build temples in far places; they know every place in the Magic, Faerie and Mundane Realms (pp. 73-74).

The Gateways (p. 73). A true gateway is two cross-lintels cut in ritual from one stone and enchanted as bridges to the spirit realm. A serpent, bought with gifts of vis, joins them: called from before a lintel, it stretches a mouth over each gate, and travellers pass quickly through it. It can bar any gate by person or oath-sworn group, but cannot perceive motive, so coercion and magical compulsion deceive it. The lore passed from Thoth's priests through the Cult of Mercury to the Order as the Hermes Portal ritual, in a weaker form.

Ealasaid rebuilt it as Hermetic thaumaturgy, in notes the magi may recover. Cut unquarried stone free in ritual, carry it to a laboratory unseen and untouched by the ritually unclean, split it, open each half as an invested device and invest a level 40 Rego Vim effect that calls the serpent and opens the bridge. Then summon a serpent. She learned 16 of the sixty names and wrote spells for three, at level 55, in her and Macomb's grimoire.

Daemonic Adjuration of [Name], Serpent of Thoth (ReVi Gen, Special, Special, Individual, Ritual). The Fourth Edition printing: stress die + Com + spell level + Penetration + Aura against stress die + 40; each point of margin counts toward the serpent's appearing, which it does when the points pass its Might. Repeat casts add up, but are lost at the next sunrise or sunset. It then bargains: 20 pawns, and 20 more for each gateway pair it already serves, reduced by half a roll of Com + Bargain + Theurgy + stress die. Under The Mysteries, casting from text needs Hermetic Theurgy equal to the spell's magnitude; otherwise a magus learns it and must master it first. A serpent serves any number of gates, one at a time. The joined gatestones stop being Arcane Connections to each other.
